tree_branches.name: Tunra
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Tunra
tree_branches.text: Ms SONIA HORNERY ( Wallsend ) —The University of Newcastle Research Associates [TUNRA] Bulk Solids, established in 1975, was the brainchild of Emeritus Professor Allan Roberts, with the aim of facilitating research and consulting services in bulk materials handling. Staff numbers rose as the flow properties laboratories at the campus took shape and developed into a world-renowned facility. TUNRA is improving industry through research, enabling business, industry, and government to connect with experts on consulting and contract research projects, specialised testing services and industry training and short courses. They also provide geotechnical services and bulk materials solutions for industry, offer a platform for various projects and leverage the experience of experts across our specialised divisions and the University of Newcastle. TUNRA offers several awards and scholarships, including the TUNRA Bulk Solids Prize for Best Performance, the A.W. Roberts Award, and the TUNRA Bulk Solids Engineering Scholarship. Additionally, TUNRA supports industry-funded scholarships and research investments within the University. Congratulations on finding solutions to problems and for the prominent ground-breaking work that you do in our community.

tree_branches.name: Ms SONIA HORNERY

tree_branches.name: Cronulla Triathlon Club
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Cronulla Triathlon Club
tree_branches.text: Mr MARK SPEAKMAN ( Cronulla ) —I highlight the success of Cronulla Triathlon Club's team at the 2025 World Triathlon Championship Finals in Wollongong last month. The club had a record 38 athletes representing five countries and about 20 volunteers and technical officers helping at the event. The Cronulla team had many achievements over the four days, including four gold medals. Leading the way was double world champion Michellie Jones who won the standard and sprint distance events in the 55 to 59 age category. In the 80 plus aquabike category, Janice Iredale showed remarkable endurance and spirit to win a gold medal. Erin Hargrave was the club's other world champion as part of the successful mixed relay squad. The club also celebrated a second placing for Kevin Robertson, second and fifth placings for Kyle Mason, third for Morgan Pike and two fifth placings for Petra Fransen. I congratulate these athletes on their success and everyone from Cronulla Triathlon Club who competed. The club is proud of the efforts of its athletes with president Adam Stroud saying "The range of ages, disciplines and levels of success shows the strength of our club multi culture and the commitment of our members."

tree_branches.name: Mr MARK SPEAKMAN

tree_branches.name: Cronulla RSL Football Club
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Cronulla RSL Football Club
tree_branches.text: Mr MARK SPEAKMAN ( Cronulla ) —I recognise everyone at Cronulla RSL Football Club who contributed to the Stingrays winning the Sutherland Shire Football Association [SSFA] champion club for junior men's football. Thanks to the efforts of players, officials and all volunteer helpers from the under 9s to under 21s, the club was awarded the Bill McIlveen Memorial Cup at the SSFA end of season presentation dinner having amassed the highest points tally of all clubs during the season. Leading the Stingrays' success in junior men's football were the U18Bs premiers, the U13D and U16D teams who competed in grand finals and the U13E boys who were finalists. I highlight the efforts of Blake Klaassen who won the club's coach of the year award aged 17 for the amazing job he did leading the U13Es to the finals. The Stingrays also celebrated special recognition for the U12C side that won SSFA's award for most improved team. Congratulations to the Cronulla RSL Football Club on achieving top club in men's juniors. I acknowledge the efforts of the club's executive and committee members to make it a successful season: Justin Cavdarovski, David Robb, Bridget Fazio, Jodie Parker, Rod Kelloway and Peter Peachey.

tree_branches.name: Mr MARK SPEAKMAN

tree_branches.name: Caringbah Redbacks Football Club
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Caringbah Redbacks Football Club
tree_branches.text: Mr MARK SPEAKMAN ( Cronulla ) —I congratulate Caringbah Redbacks Football Club for being honoured as the 2025 Sutherland Shire Football Association [SSFA] champion club for senior women's football. The Redbacks proudly received the Stan Ellis Memorial Cup at the SSFA's end of season presentation dinner as champion club participating in the all age women, over 30 and over 40 competitions. Driving the club's success in women's football this year were the premiership winning W21B team, the Premier League Women team as runners up and WSDs who were finalists. I know winning this title means a lot to the Redbacks club which has made women's football a priority. Well done to the club on the pathway it's building for the next generation of women's footballers. I acknowledge president Andy Neudegg and the club's committee for their enthusiasm for growing women's football and I join them in recognising every player, coach, volunteer and member who made winning the award possible. It's one of many highlights in a very successful 65th season for the Redbacks.

tree_branches.name: Mr MARK SPEAKMAN

tree_branches.name: Peek-A-Boo Cottage
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Peek-A-Boo Cottage
tree_branches.text: Mr JAMES GRIFFIN ( Manly ) —I rise to congratulate the entire team at Peek-A-Boo Cottage in Seaforth, who have recently been announced as a winner at the Excellence in Early Childhood Education Awards, taking home the 2025 Outcomes for Children (Birth–3 Years) Award. Since 2008, this family-owned centre has provided exceptional care for children aged 0 to 2 in a warm, home-like environment. Peek-A-Boo Cottage is known for its personalised approach, recognising that every child and every family is unique, and that the earliest years lay the foundation for lifelong learning. Their dedicated team of educators consistently goes above and beyond to create a nurturing space where children feel safe, supported and encouraged to grow. I congratulate Peek-A-Boo Cottage on this well-deserved honour and thank them for their outstanding contribution to early childhood education in the Manly Electorate.

tree_branches.name: Manly SES Unit - Tsunami Awareness Initiative
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Manly SES Unit - Tsunami Awareness Initiative
tree_branches.text: Mr JAMES GRIFFIN ( Manly ) —Mr Speaker, I rise to once more recognise the outstanding work of the Manly SES Unit for their recent community outreach campaign to raise awareness about tsunami safety on the Northern Beaches. In the lead-up to World Tsunami Awareness Day, Manly SES volunteers engaged with residents about a natural hazard that is rare, but real, and one that has impacted the NSW coastline more than 40 times in the past two centuries. Through community stalls, conversation and nearly a thousand sausage sandwiches, volunteers helped locals understand evacuation routes, warning signs and what to do if a tsunami alert is issued. More than 50 committed members letterbox-dropped information around the electorate, answered questions and ensured our community is better prepared - whether at home, at the beach or travelling abroad. I commend the Manly SES Unit for their hard work and dedication to keeping our community safe and informed.

tree_branches.name: Mr JAMES GRIFFIN
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Manly SES Unit - Tsunami Awareness Initiative > Mr JAMES GRIFFIN

tree_branches.name: Eleanor Eakins
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Eleanor Eakins
tree_branches.text: Mr JAMES GRIFFIN ( Manly ) —Mr Speaker, I recognise Eleanor Eakins, a pillar of the Stony Range Botanic Garden in Dee Why who has devoted herself to its care for nearly forty years. Since 1986, Eleanor has nurtured this treasured community garden, serving as its Honorary Secretary for 28 years until her retirement at the end of 2024. Her leadership, commitment, and extraordinary efforts have been integral to preserving and enhancing Stony Range so that it continues to thrive as beautiful green space in the heart of industrial Dee Why. Eleanor's contributions extend well beyond the garden. Through her long involvement with the Girl Guides over many years, she has helped empower generations of girls and young women to discover their potential and develop as leaders. Eleanor is deeply respected by her peers and admired by all who have had the privilege of working and volunteering alongside her. I thank her for her service and remarkable dedication to our local environment and community.

tree_branches.name: Mr JAMES GRIFFIN
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Eleanor Eakins > Mr JAMES GRIFFIN

tree_branches.name: Tahlia Marsh
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Tahlia Marsh
tree_branches.text: Mr RICHIE WILLIAMSON ( Clarence ) —Congratulations must go to Clarence Valley's Tahlia Marsh, who has once again proven herself to be at the top of her game when it comes to BMX. Tahlia took out the State Champion title in both the 17–24 Years Women's Category and 17-24 Years Women's Cruiser Category at the 2025 AusCycling BMX Racing State Championships. Held at the Castle Hill BMX Club in north-west Sydney in September, the event brought together the state's best riders, and Tahlia shone brightly on the track. After Tahlia dominated in her heats and semi-final, she stormed through the final in under 32 seconds to claim victory in the Women's Category — an incredible achievement against a field of 17 talented competitors. This occasion marks the second time Tahlia, a member of the Clarence Valley BMX Club, has claimed the prestigious title, having previously won in 2022. In addition to this great achievement, for the second year in a row, Tahlia was selected as a coach for the Australian Mighty 11's Team. The Mighty 11s is an international BMX competition between Australia and New Zealand. Your passion for BMX is inspiring Tahlia. Congratulations and well done on your outstanding successes so far.

tree_branches.name: Mr RICHIE WILLIAMSON
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Tahlia Marsh > Mr RICHIE WILLIAMSON

tree_branches.name: North Coast Electrical
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > North Coast Electrical
tree_branches.text: Mr RICHIE WILLIAMSON ( Clarence ) —I would like to mention and congratulate North Coast Electrical on their attendance at the NSW National Electrical and Communications Association [NECA] awards for 2025, held in Sydney in August. The NECA Awards program is the electrical and communications industry's highest accolade. The Awards celebrate innovation, craftsmanship and excellence across the entire electrical and communications industry. North Coast Electrical were selected as a finalist in the Emerging Small Business category and walked away with the Highly Commended award, placing second in the entire state. North Coast Electrical service Maclean, Yamba, Grafton and surrounding areas and complete residential, commercial and industrial works. As a family owned and operated business, being recognised among the best in the field while surrounded by 600 plus industry professionals is a remarkable achievement. Congratulations to director James Priest and the entire team on your continued hard work that resulted in achieving such a great result. Well done North Coast Electrical team, I'm sure there will be more awards in the future.

tree_branches.name: Mr RICHIE WILLIAMSON
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > North Coast Electrical > Mr RICHIE WILLIAMSON

tree_branches.name: Benjamin Benn
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Benjamin Benn
tree_branches.text: Mr RICHIE WILLIAMSON ( Clarence ) —I would like to congratulate Benjamin Benn, who has recently celebrated a remarkable milestone of 25 years of employment with Casino Food Company. Benny's story is one of dedication, growth, and genuine Casino Food Company spirit. Benny's early days with the company started out on the processing floors before he spent some time as part of the customer service team. Benny quickly became known for his friendly nature and built exceptional rapport with both colleagues and customers. Today, Benny makes up part of the company's accounting team in Business Analysis. Benny's continued positive attitude and energy have seen him successful across all of his roles with Casino Food Company. His ability to connect with people and bring positivity to every interaction has shaped him into a standout presence throughout his journey at the business. Benny's dedication not only contributes to the success of Casino Food Company but also strengthens the broader business community through the example it sets, with milestones like this reminding us of the lasting value of loyalty, teamwork, and continuous personal growth. Congratulations Benny, on your 25 years and I wish you all the success in the years ahead.

tree_branches.name: Cabramatta Buddhist Community Premier's Reception In NSW Parliament House
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Cabramatta Buddhist Community Premier's Reception In NSW Parliament House
tree_branches.text: Mr TRI VO ( Cabramatta ) —I had the great honour and privilege of hosting the Cabramatta Buddhist Community Premier's Reception in NSW Parliament House on 18 September 2025. Buddhism is the second‑largest religion in my Cabramatta electorate, with approximately 22,800 followers. The reception celebrated the significant influence of Buddhism on the harmonious social fabric of our community. At least Fourteen major Buddhist temples and organisations from diverse cultural backgrounds came together in a united, cross-cultural gathering in NSW Parliament House, the first of its kind in our Electorate's history. I extend my sincere appreciation to all who participated. Special thanks go to the spiritual leaders who offered prayers and blessings, and to Bhikkhuni Thich Nu Giac Anh and the dedicated volunteers from Phap Bao Pagoda for their kindness and the beautiful decorations. I also thank Premier Chris Minns for his continued support. Events like these remind us of the timeless Buddhist values of kindness, compassion, and interconnectedness, which guide and inspire peaceful coexistence and harmony in our multicultural society. May these values continue to guide and inspire us all.

tree_branches.name: Mr TRI VO

tree_branches.name: St Barnabas Anglican Church
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > St Barnabas Anglican Church
tree_branches.text: Mr TRI VO ( Cabramatta ) —On the 14th of September 2025, I had the privilege of visiting the St Barnabas Anglican Church in Bossley Park, which resides in my Cabramatta Electorate. I had the privilege to meet and speak with Senior Minister, Reverand Stephen Shead, about their successful application of the Community Building Partnership grants. St Barnabas Anglican Church resides in both Fairfield and Bossley Park, with the Fairfield branch being founded during the early 1960s and the Bossley Park branch being an addition to the organisation. The organisation holds services for the local parishioners, while also hosting community events to provide a support network for the youth and members of the community that are struggling. I also had the pleasure of attending the morning service that was held by Senior Minister, Reverand Stephen Shead. Their morning sermon highlighted the importance of honouring the people that are in our daily life and how respect and upholding values are fundamental in achieving this. I congratulate the Senior Minister and the Church on their successful application and look forward to their continued contribution in providing a place of prayer and spiritual guidance to our local community.

tree_branches.name: Mr TRI VO
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > St Barnabas Anglican Church > Mr TRI VO

tree_branches.name: Miss Compassionate 2025
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Miss Compassionate 2025
tree_branches.text: Mr TRI VO ( Cabramatta ) —I congratulate Miss Compassionate on the success of their 2025 Pageant and on the 5th Anniversary. Miss Compassionate is far more than a beauty pageant. It promotes the core values of kindness, compassion, and inner strength. Each year, participants are encouraged to turn these values into action, supporting charitable work, standing for humanity, and raising awareness of important social issues, including human rights. It was a privilege to serve as one of the judges this year, and to see the devoted effort each contestant brought to their respective projects and community initiatives. I congratulate all contestants and the winners for their commitment to making a positive difference in their communities. I wish to acknowledge Ms Thao Le, the founder and organiser of Miss Compassionate, for her tireless work in growing this meaningful initiative. I wish Miss Compassionate continued success in their endeavours to promote compassion and kindness through actions in the years ahead.

tree_branches.name: Mr TRI VO

tree_branches.name: Donna Douglas
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Donna Douglas
tree_branches.text: Mrs TANYA THOMPSON ( Myall Lakes ) —I rise today to acknowledge Donna Douglas, the dedicated force behind Donna's Kitchen, for her exceptional service to our community following the recent flood event and as we move into the Christmas season. Donna's Kitchen began as a simple but heartfelt vision to provide home‑cooked meals, care-packages, and essential support to those experiencing hardship. It has now grown into a trusted and compassionate community hub for individuals and families who are doing it tough, including the elderly, the isolated, and those facing unexpected challenges. In the immediate aftermath of the floods, Donna mobilised local support with remarkable speed and generosity. She coordinated food donations, established accessible collection points for non-perishables, and opened her own home as a place of comfort, connection, and practical assistance for those affected. As Christmas approaches, Donna continues her tireless efforts — gathering donations, organising meals, and ensuring that no member of our community is left without support, dignity, or companionship during what can be a difficult time for many. I commend Donna for her unwavering commitment, compassionate leadership, and extraordinary contribution to the wellbeing of the Manning Valley community.

tree_branches.name: Mrs TANYA THOMPSON
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Donna Douglas > Mrs TANYA THOMPSON

tree_branches.name: Elliott Simpson
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Elliott Simpson
tree_branches.text: Mrs TANYA THOMPSON ( Myall Lakes ) —I rise to recognise an outstanding young member of our community, Elliott Simpson from the Green Point Rural Fire Brigade, who has been named the NSW RFS Young Volunteer of the Year in the 16–25 years category. Since joining the Brigade Elliott has attended more than 160 callouts, an extraordinary contribution for someone so young. His service includes deployments during the 2025 Cyclone Alfred event and the Taree flood recovery efforts, where he worked alongside experienced volunteers to support communities in their time of greatest need. Elliott is not only committed on the ground but is also passionate about growing as a leader within the Service. He attended the Young Member Leadership College in 2024 and the Young Members Forum in 2025, demonstrating his desire to strengthen his skills and contribute to the future of the RFS. In recent years, Elliott has generously given his time to assist with district training courses, helping to develop the next generation of volunteers. He is now completing his Crew Leader qualifications—a testament to his capability, dedication, and drive. I congratulate Elliott on this well-deserved recognition.

tree_branches.name: Mrs TANYA THOMPSON

tree_branches.name: Australian National Busking Championships
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Australian National Busking Championships
tree_branches.text: Mr STEVE WHAN ( Monaro — Minister for Skills, TAFE and Tertiary Education ) —I'd like to congratulate local brothers Filipe and Justin Klempfner for winning the people's choice award at the Australian National Busking Championships in Cooma last weekend, and Justin himself taking home the second-place trophy in the finals of the primary age category. Filipe and Justin are Berridale locals, The K Brothers, and impressed the crowd with their country and folk violin skills. Now in its 14th year, the Australian National Busking Championships runs over two days and brings in musicians and tourists from all over Australia. None of this would be possible without the work founder Allan Spencer and volunteers put in each year. Allan has run Cooma Music with his partner Leslie for decades, and it's a pillar of the region's musical community. With support from the local community, this year had over $14,000 in prizemoney and prizes up for grabs. Well done to all the competitors, and here's to another 14 years and beyond.

tree_branches.name: Mr STEVE WHAN

tree_branches.name: Delegate & Michelago Public Schools at the State Athletic Championships
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Delegate & Michelago Public Schools at the State Athletic Championships
tree_branches.text: Mr STEVE WHAN ( Monaro — Minister for Skills, TAFE and Tertiary Education ) —Last month, students from Delegate and Michelago Public Schools travelled to Sydney to compete at the NSW PSSA Athletics Championships. The PSSA is the pinnacle of public school sport in NSW and a great opportunity for young athletes from our country schools. I want to pay tribute to the principals of the schools, Mr Bannister from Delegate and Mr Smith from Michelago, who not only drove their students all the way to Sydney but also to Wollongong for the Regional Championships. Achievements like this truly show how small and regional public schools punch well above their weight – and they show the great commitment of our wonderful staff. Congratulations to all the students and teachers involved!

tree_branches.name: Joanna Roweth
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Joanna Roweth
tree_branches.text: Mr PAUL TOOLE ( Bathurst ) —This statement is to acknowledge the achievements of Blayney High School student Joanna Roweth. Joanna is a bright young lady with a bubbly personality and a natural talent for writing. Joanna recently entered the 2025 Slam Poetry Competition. Out of 600 entries state-wide Joanna was within the top 60 competitors heading into regional finals. Joanna won the Slam Poetry section of the regional finals in Dubbo and will now go on to the State final held at Taronga Zoo. Her poem titled "For the Wild" addresses the concepts of conservation, the environment, animals, wild habitats and a sustainable future. Congratulations Joanna on such an impressive achievement and the Blayney region is right behind you, cheering you on for state finals later this year.

tree_branches.name: Mr PAUL TOOLE

tree_branches.text: Mr PAUL TOOLE ( Bathurst ) —This statement is to acknowledge the achievements of Wallerawang Public School's outstanding 2025 school captains, Ruby, Ryley, Audrey and Wilson. As a representative of our community, Ruby, Ryley, Audrey and Wilson have led with enthusiasm and humility and the commitment shown by these four students has been truly exceptional. Throughout this year, Ruby, Ryley, Audrey and Wilson have embodied the very best qualities of leadership: service, integrity and teamwork. They have represented their peers with pride, supported staff and students alike and worked hard to make this school an even better place to learn and grow. Whether speaking at assemblies, helping to organise school events, or lending a hand to those who needed support, they have shown that leadership is about lifting others up. As they graduate and take their next steps into High School, I have no doubt that the skills, confidence and compassion they've shown here will take them far. On behalf of our wider community, I want to thank you for your contribution, congratulate you on your achievements and wish you every success for the future.

tree_branches.name: Camden Show Ball
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Camden Show Ball
tree_branches.text: Mrs JUDY HANNAN ( Wollondilly ) —For over 139 years, Camden Show Society has been a proud part of the Camden community and is one of the oldest show societies in Australia. I was honoured to attend Camden Show Ball again this year and share in the wonderful traditions. A key part of its commitment to the community is its long-standing support for young women through the Young Woman of the Year Competition. Held annually for more than 60 years, this competition recognises and celebrates the ambition, confidence, knowledge, and community spirit of young women. Entrants are judged on personality, presentation, public speaking, and volunteering history qualities that reflect leadership and a passion for rural life and agriculture. Each year, one young woman is selected to represent the Camden district at the zone level, with the opportunity to progress to the state finals. Through this experience, all participants gain valuable personal and professional development and become ambassadors for their community and the agricultural industry. I would like to congratulate all those who enter and recognise their courage to aim high and follow their dreams. Every participant leaves the competition with new skills, connections, and confidence.

tree_branches.name: Mrs JUDY HANNAN

tree_branches.name: Macarthur Mayoral Charity Night
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Macarthur Mayoral Charity Night
tree_branches.text: Mrs JUDY HANNAN ( Wollondilly ) —It was a great night on Friday at the Macarthur Mayors' Charity Dinner, held at the newly transformed restored and revitalised Camden Civic Centre, with fantastic entertainment and plenty of familiar faces from across Wollondilly and the Macarthur region. Events like this are all about celebrating, connecting, and most importantly, raising vital funds to support Kids of Macarthur Health Foundation, helping provide essential paediatric medical equipment and services for local children and their families. Congratulations to Denise McGrath! Who was recognised for an incredible 25 years with Kids of Macarthur Health Foundation. Well done to the Mayors for putting on such a great night! It was awesome to see Councillors and Mayors coming together for charity. Thank you to Wollondilly Mayor Matt Gould, Campbelltown Mayor Darcy Lound and Camden Mayor Therese Fedeli for representing all three shires and putting on a great night.

tree_branches.name: Mrs JUDY HANNAN

tree_branches.name: The Right Start Foundation Fifteenth Anniversary
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > The Right Start Foundation Fifteenth Anniversary
tree_branches.text: Mrs JUDY HANNAN ( Wollondilly ) —On Saturday night we celebrated The Right Start Foundation's fifteenth Anniversary — and what a beautiful, fun and joy-filled evening it was! The Foundation has been supporting families who have a child with Down Syndrome for fifteen years, and it was wonderful to see so many familiar faces, including volunteers and former board members. The Right Start Foundation is a charitable organization that supports families of children with Down syndrome by providing them with essential resources, therapies, and support networks to help them get the "right start in life". We were treated to a heartfelt performance by the children and young people the Foundation supports. A huge congratulations to founder Glenda Graban and her incredible team for reaching this milestone. Thank you to everyone who came along to support The Right Start — here's to many more years of making a difference.

tree_branches.name: Mrs JUDY HANNAN

tree_branches.name: St Anne's Preschool
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > St Anne's Preschool
tree_branches.text: Ms JULIA FINN ( Granville ) —I was delighted to represent the NSW Government at the official opening of the renovated St Anne's Preschool in Merrylands in my electorate on 30 October 2025, an important reminder of the vital role community-run preschools play in giving children the best possible start. The NSW Government invested $151,950 through the Capital Works Grants Program to create additional preschool places and deliver upgraded learning spaces, ensuring more local families can access quality early education close to home. Merrylands has a long tradition of service, education and community leadership - from Sister Edith Faber, who served as a nurse in World War I - to generations of outstanding local educators who have shaped the lives of local children. St Anne's Preschool continues this legacy, supporting families from diverse cultural backgrounds and helping young learners build confidence, curiosity and friendships in their earliest years. I acknowledge the leadership of Director Vanessa Bentley, staff, families and the community volunteers who worked tirelessly to complete this renovation, and thank Reverend Rodney Kerr and Gina Grimes for their contributions to this milestone. I commend everyone involved for their dedication to the children of Merrylands and the ongoing story of this proud community.

tree_branches.name: Ms JULIA FINN
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > St Anne's Preschool > Ms JULIA FINN

tree_branches.name: Granville Public School Diwali
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Granville Public School Diwali
tree_branches.text: Ms JULIA FINN ( Granville ) —I was delighted to attend the inaugural Diwali celebration held at Granville Public School in my electorate on 4 November 2025, a significant milestone in the school's 144‑year history and a reflection of the rich cultural diversity that defines the Granville community. Diwali, the Festival of Lights, is celebrated across many faiths and traditions, yet its central message that light triumphs over darkness, knowledge over ignorance, and good over evil resonates deeply across our multicultural society. Granville Public School, like so many in Western Sydney, brings together students and families from Indian, Nepalese, Sri Lankan, Pakistani, Fijian and many other backgrounds. This celebration demonstrates how cultural events in our schools build understanding, respect and social cohesion from an early age. I particularly acknowledge Principal Mrs Davis, the teaching staff, parents and volunteers who worked together to bring Diwali to the school community in such a meaningful and joyful way. Their efforts highlight the vital role schools play as places of shared learning, cultural pride and collective celebration. I extend warm wishes to all families marking Diwali and commend Granville Public School for fostering a spirit of unity, respect and cultural celebration.

tree_branches.name: Ms JULIA FINN
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Granville Public School Diwali > Ms JULIA FINN

tree_branches.name: Darulfatwa, the Islamic High Council of Australia
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Darulfatwa, the Islamic High Council of Australia
tree_branches.text: Ms JULIA FINN ( Granville ) —I acknowledge the important work undertaken at the Community Response to Domestic and Family Violence seminar hosted by Darulfatwa, the Islamic High Council of Australia in Chester Hill on 9 October. Domestic and family violence remains one of the most pressing social challenges across Western Sydney, affecting women, children and families in every cultural, linguistic and faith community. I commend Darulfatwa, under the leadership of Manager Mohamad Chams, for convening this forum and for their ongoing commitment to peace, justice and the wellbeing of local families. By bringing together religious leaders, NSW Police, the Department of Communities and Justice, MetroAssist and Justice Support Centre, the seminar reflected the collective responsibility required to prevent violence and support survivors. The NSW Government is strengthening this work through the Pathways to Prevention: NSW Strategy for the Prevention of Domestic, Family and Sexual Violence 2024–2028 and a $5.2 million investment in community-led prevention programs that promote respectful relationships, healthy masculinities, consent education and gender equality. I thank all involved for their leadership and commitment to building safer, stronger and more respectful communities across Western Sydney.

tree_branches.name: Ms JULIA FINN
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Darulfatwa, the Islamic High Council of Australia > Ms JULIA FINN

tree_branches.name: The Bruns Brekkie
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > The Bruns Brekkie
tree_branches.text: Ms TAMARA SMITH ( Ballina ) —Today I acknowledge The Bruns Brekkie, a volunteer-led community initiative that provides care, nourishment and connection for people doing it tough in Brunswick Heads and surrounding areas. Twice each week, dedicated volunteers serve toasties, coffee, fresh fruit and take-home meals, supported by generous contributions from the Bruns Bakery, Sunday Sustainable Bakery and Liberation Larder. What began as a simple breakfast offering has grown into a warm and welcoming community space where pensioners, single parents, isolated seniors and people experiencing homelessness can gather, share a meal and feel supported. The Bruns Brekkie team has also created a vital support hub. On Fridays, the Orange Sky van provides free laundry and showers, alongside visiting mental health and housing services, ensuring people can access dignity, safety and practical assistance in one place. After losing their original home, the group was generously welcomed by Our Lady of Lourdes Catholic Church, whose support has allowed Bruns Brekkie to continue operating in the heart of Brunswick Heads. I wholeheartedly commend coordinator John Dale, volunteers Melissa Barnes, Patricia Warren and all who contribute. Their compassion, consistency and inclusiveness strengthen our community immeasurably and ensure no one is left behind.

tree_branches.name: Ms TAMARA SMITH
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > The Bruns Brekkie > Ms TAMARA SMITH

tree_branches.name: NSW Rural Fire Service Alstonville/wollongbar Brigade
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > NSW Rural Fire Service Alstonville/wollongbar Brigade
tree_branches.text: Ms TAMARA SMITH ( Ballina ) —Today I recognise the Alstonville/Wollongbar Brigade paying special mention to members honoured at the RFS Far North Coast Medal Presentation. Senior Deputy Captain Corey Gray received the National Medal for 15 years diligent service, acknowledging his exceptional commitment and leadership. Patrick Higgins, now Captain of the Brigade, received the National Medal for 25 years diligent service and the National Medal 1st Clasp, marking his service across the Blue Mountains and the Northern Rivers, including several major disaster responses. Malcolm Johnson was awarded the 35 years diligent service National Medal, National Medal 1st and 2nd Clasps and Long Service Medal 2nd Clasp, recognising his long-standing operational excellence, involvement in several interstate emergency responses and his contribution to the Brigade in several key leadership roles. Ray Wood received the National Medal for 10 years diligent service, reflecting his strong dedication to training, operational preparedness and community protection. Collectively, these members represent the strength and resilience of the Alstonville/Wollongbar Brigade. Their combined decades of service and commitment to supporting new volunteers embody the very best of the NSW RFS. I commend them all for their professionalism, courage and dedication to safeguarding our community.

tree_branches.name: Ms TAMARA SMITH

tree_branches.name: Elke Lysaght
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Elke Lysaght
tree_branches.text: Ms YASMIN CATLEY ( Swansea — Minister for Police and Counter-terrorism, and Minister for the Hunter ) —Speaker, I rise to acknowledge Elke Lysaght of Swansea High School, who was part of a contingent of students from Swansea High School to take part in the University of Newcastle's Annual Youth Forum. On 11 September 2025, Elke attended NSW Parliament to participate in the Youth Forum that was run by the University of Newcastle's Centre for Law and Social Justice, along with the Australian Lawyers for Human Rights. The topic of the Youth Forum was human rights protection for New South Wales. The Forum brough together 60 high school students from 21 schools in the Hunter and Sydney regions. The students engaged with each other to discuss what a Human Rights Act for NSW should include. Thank you to the University of Newcastle and the Australian Lawyers for Human Rights for hosting the Youth Forum and allowing students to participate in political life. Thank you also to the teachers from Swansea High that supported students to attend the Youth Forum. Congratulations to Elke for attending the Youth Forum and making your voice heard to all parliamentarians.

tree_branches.name: Aelite Dental Business of the Year 2025 Bayside Local Business Awards
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Aelite Dental Business of the Year 2025 Bayside Local Business Awards
tree_branches.text: Mr CHRIS MINNS ( Kogarah — Premier ) —I wish to congratulate Aelite Dental on being named the Business of the Year at the 2025 Bayside Local Business Awards. Aelite Dental has been serving the Kogarah community for over 20 years, providing professional dental care that suits individual patient needs. By integrating exceptional personalised care for each patient, they have created a relaxed environment for patients undergoing dental care. They use exceptional state-of-the-art technology to ensure every patient's wellbeing, providing beautiful smiles to the community. Having completed over a thousand surgeries, they are experts in their field, and winning this award is a testament to the exemplary service they provide. Once again, I wish to congratulate Aeilte Dental on being recognised as Business of the Year at the Bayside Local Business awards. I wish Aelite Dental every success and thank them for the service they provide to the community.

tree_branches.name: Mr CHRIS MINNS

tree_branches.name: The Magnificals Chamber Orchestra
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > The Magnificals Chamber Orchestra
tree_branches.text: Mr CHRIS MINNS ( Kogarah — Premier ) —I wish to congratulate The Magnificals Chamber Orchestra for their tireless work to break barriers in the music industry, providing accessible performance opportunities for everyone. The Magnificals Chamber Orchestra is all about opportunity, striving to make sure that future musicians have access to any avenues of opportunity to grow their career. They also aim to support mothers who are professional musicians, who, for various reasons, have had to pause or change careers while raising their families. With their flexibility-based approach, they increase access to equitable participation, as well as being a practice orchestra for local emerging conductors and composers. The Magnificals is not just for mothers, nor is it an all‑female collective. It is simply a place where anyone who might need that extra opportunity, can find a space to belong, whether young or old, emerging or experienced professional, at any stage of their music career. Their group is diverse, including tertiary music students, conservatorium graduates, mature-aged professionals, as well as traditional ethnic musicians. Once again, I would like to commend the Magnificals Chamber Orchestra for uplifting current and future musicians in our local community.

tree_branches.name: Mr CHRIS MINNS
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > The Magnificals Chamber Orchestra > Mr CHRIS MINNS

tree_branches.name: Autism Community Network
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Autism Community Network
tree_branches.text: Mr CHRIS MINNS ( Kogarah — Premier ) —I wish to commend Autism Community Network [CAN] on hosting a free high tea for carers this October. Supported by the Benevolent Society and Carers Gateway, they welcomed 120 carers for a morning of celebration and recognition of the great work carers do. Being a carer is a demanding job, and this high tea recognised the sacrifices that are made by carers across our community to provide aid to those in need. This event was about encouraging self-care and bonding over common experiences, swapping stories, the good and the bad. The ACN has experienced growing demand for their specialised autistic care services, starting additional groups and supporting more families. Once again, I would like to thank Autism Community Network for hosting a free high tea to support and congratulate the hard-working carers in Kogarah.

tree_branches.name: Mr CHRIS MINNS

tree_branches.name: Australian International Academy Student Leadership Elections
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Australian International Academy Student Leadership Elections
tree_branches.text: Mr JASON LI ( Strathfield ) —I rise to recognise the students of the Australian International Academy in Strathfield South for their student leader election process. This annual event reflects the school's commitment to student voice, civic responsibility and active participation in democratic life. This year the election process mirrored a formal NSW ballot, giving students valuable hands-on experience with voting procedures and reinforcing fairness and transparency in decision making. I was pleased to attend and observe part of the process and was impressed by the energy and interest shown by the student community. Their engagement reflects a strong culture that encourages leadership, representation and respectful participation. I commend and congratulate all students who nominated, including Manahil Amir, Zahra Afzal and Mona Taleb, who was successfully elected as School Captain. I wish all AIA's student leaders every success in the year ahead. I also commend AIA's staff including School Principal Bedrieh Kheir and Deputy Principal Ossama Harris for their guidance and support. The spirit shown by these students reminds us that democracy is strongest when young people are empowered to learn it, practise it and lead it.

tree_branches.name: Mr JASON LI

tree_branches.name: Burwood Greek Street Fair
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Burwood Greek Street Fair
tree_branches.text: Mr JASON LI ( Strathfield ) —I rise to recognise the tremendous success of this year's Burwood Greek Street Fair, a much-loved celebration that continues to highlight Burwood as one of Sydney's most culturally diverse and welcoming communities. The Fair brings the vibrant spirit and timeless tradition of the outdoor Greek panigiri, a centuries-old festival, to the heart of Sydney and it has rightly become one of Burwood's most anticipated cultural events. The event showcased wonderful music, dance, food and family-friendly entertainment that reflected both Greek heritage and our shared community pride. I acknowledge and thank Burwood Council for its continued partnership and support and extend special recognition to The Greek Orthodox Parish and Community of Burwood and District, Saint Nectarios, whose dedication and volunteering make this celebration possible each year. It was a pleasure to attend and to witness the strong community engagement, with so many local families, businesses, schools and cultural groups joining together in such a joyful atmosphere. My warm congratulations and thanks go to everyone involved, and I look forward to celebrating again next year.

tree_branches.name: Mr JASON LI
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Burwood Greek Street Fair > Mr JASON LI

tree_branches.name: Cost of Living Hub
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Cost of Living Hub
tree_branches.text: Mr JASON LI ( Strathfield ) —I rise to recognise the Cost of Living Help Hub held on 10 November at Homebush Public School, organised in collaboration with federal representative Sally Sitou and a strong line‑up of support services. The Cost of Living Hub is held on a regular basis, and bring together residents with representatives from Service NSW, Centrelink/Services Australia, Sydney Water, Vinnies, and local community legal centres including the Marrickville Legal Centre. The Hub provides a valuable opportunity for people to bring their latest utility bills, ask directly about rebates and vouchers and talk one-on-one with experts about ways to ease cost pressures in our households. I thank all the service organisations, their staff and volunteers and every community member who came along. Your engagement ensures that our community is better informed, better connected and better supported in these challenging times. Together we are making sure cost-of-living support is accessible, practical and responsive in the Strathfield electorate.

tree_branches.name: Mr JASON LI
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Cost of Living Hub > Mr JASON LI

tree_branches.name: Bravery and Betrayal Screening In Parliament
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Bravery and Betrayal Screening In Parliament
tree_branches.text: Mr MARK COURE ( Oatley ) —Speaker, I recently had the privilege of hosting alongside my colleagues, Robyn Preston MP and James Griffin MP the screening of Bravery and Betrayal at the Theatrette, here in Parliament. It was an honour to see the documentary which highlighted the compelling story of the Australian SAS in Afghanistan. Following the tragedy of 9/11, Australian soldiers were deployed to ensure our country's safety, enduring great struggles and sacrifice in the face of danger. The documentary includes inspiring interviews with both the SAS soldiers and their families as well as personal insights from our past Prime Ministers, Hon. Dr Kevin Rudd AC, Hon. John Howard OM AC and Hon. Tony Abbott AC. It was an incredibly moving and powerful experience, helping Australians to connect and showcase their appreciation for our brave soldiers. Documentaries like these remind us of the bravery and dedication Australian soldiers showcase on a daily basis, highlighting the commitment and strength needed to serve our country with honour and courage. I'd like to thank the outstanding team behind this amazing documentary for their work in bringing these important stories to light.

tree_branches.name: Mr MARK COURE
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Bravery and Betrayal Screening In Parliament > Mr MARK COURE

tree_branches.name: Macedonian Festival of Sydney 2025
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Macedonian Festival of Sydney 2025
tree_branches.text: Mr MARK COURE ( Oatley ) —Speaker, I recently had the fantastic opportunity to join the Macedonian community at Carss Park to celebrate the 2025 Macedonian Festival of Sydney. It was incredible to see our diverse community embrace Macedonia's vibrant traditions, displaying the richness of their culture through traditional music, folk dances and delicious food. For many generations, the Macedonian community has been crucial in shaping the cultural, economic and civic life of New South Wales. They are a pillar in our community, demonstrating unity and pride through their work to preserve Macedonian culture and traditions. From cultural performances to traditional dances, food and speeches, this was a fun and exciting day out for the family. It is truly inspiring to see the great pride that our Australian-Macedonian community has in sharing their culture with others. I would like to thank the Macedonian Festival of Sydney Committee for their hard work in creating a remarkable event that truly encompasses the beauty and spirit of Macedonian culture. I look forward to next year's festival!

tree_branches.name: Mr MARK COURE
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Macedonian Festival of Sydney 2025 > Mr MARK COURE

tree_branches.name: Mortdale RSL Sub-Branch Luncheon
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Mortdale RSL Sub-Branch Luncheon
tree_branches.text: Mr MARK COURE ( Oatley ) —Speaker, I recently had the privilege of attending Mortdale RSL Sub‑Branch's Remembrance Day luncheon to honour the sacrifices of our Australian servicemen and servicewomen. Remembrance Day is an important time when we commemorate the Armistice of 1918 when guns feel silent, marking the end of World War 1. Events like these are crucial in order to help us remember those who fought and sacrificed in order to keep our nation safe and maintain our freedom. It is also a time for us to show our gratitude towards the men and women who are currently serving in our military forces, devoting their lives to protecting our great country. RSL Sub-Branches like Mortdale, play an imperative role within our local community. Not only do they provide support to our veterans and their families, but they also ensure that our past soldiers sacrifice, and service is never forgotten. I would like to extend my thanks to the Mortdale RSL Sub-Branch for hosting an incredibly meaningful Remembrance Day luncheon. Your commitment to ensuring the memory of those who fought for Australia is truly inspiring.

tree_branches.name: Mr MARK COURE
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Mortdale RSL Sub-Branch Luncheon > Mr MARK COURE

tree_branches.name: Sydney Street Fair and Makersville Marrickville Makers Market Trail
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Sydney Street Fair and Makersville Marrickville Makers Market Trail
tree_branches.text: Ms JO HAYLEN ( Summer Hill ) —Congratulations to the organisers and neighbours behind the inaugural Sydney Street Fair and Makersville Marrickville Makers Market Trail, a celebration of creativity and community in the Inner West. On Saturday 13 December, Sydney Street Marrickville will come alive as it closes to traffic and opens to makers, artists and visitors for a day of markets, music, food trucks and free workshops. This collaborative project showcases the incredible talent and innovation of Marrickville's creative precinct, with venues including Among The Trees, Brand Furniture, Rikota Studio, sydneystreet.gallery and Wildwood Designs. The Fair offers something for everyone, from Christmas shopping at handmade stalls to performances for kids and the chance to explore the unique businesses that call Sydney Street home. The Makersville Trail extends the experience across the Inner West, connecting locals and visitors with creative spaces and makers. Thank you to all the organisers, volunteers and artists for making this vision a reality. I encourage everyone to join the festivities on 13 December and support our local artists and makers.

tree_branches.name: Ms JO HAYLEN
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Sydney Street Fair and Makersville Marrickville Makers Market Trail > Ms JO HAYLEN

tree_branches.name: Greenway Community Advocacy
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Greenway Community Advocacy
tree_branches.text: Ms JO HAYLEN ( Summer Hill ) —Congratulations and thank you to the Inner West community whose vision and persistence have delivered the GreenWay, a transformative active transport corridor linking the Cooks River to Iron Cove. The idea began decades ago with residents and bushcare advocates who imagined a green corridor along the old freight rail line, creating space for walking, cycling, bushland restoration and cultural connection. This grassroots vision became reality through the tireless efforts of so many across our community. I recognise local campaigners Alex Lofts, Bruce Ashley, Jo Blackman, Suzy Carter, Nick Chapman, Alice Hickey, Bronwyn Holland, Colin Jones, Jennifer Kent, Mary Osborn, and Councillors Mark Drury, Lucille McKenna, Jeanette Wang, Simon Emsley, Anna York, Max Phillips, Linda Eisler, Sam Byrne, Peter Olive, and former local members Carmel Tebbutt and Linda Burney, whose petition campaign galvanised thousands. Whilst these individuals matter, they represent countless thousands who campaigned, signed petitions and fought for this vision. Congratulations to Inner West Council for its commitment in delivering this project under Mayor Darcy Byrne and the many staff such as Joanne McDonald and Lauren McIver, who brought it life. The GreenWay is a victory for community activism and a legacy for future generations.

tree_branches.name: Ms JO HAYLEN
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Greenway Community Advocacy > Ms JO HAYLEN

tree_branches.name: Francis Lee
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Francis Lee
tree_branches.text: Mr RON HOENIG ( Heffron — Minister for Local Government ) —I congratulate Francis Lee of Zetland, whose short story "Kite and Water Tap" has been selected for publication in Volume 11 of Seniors' Stories, the NSW Government program honouring the creativity and lived experience of older people. Now 80 years old and soon to celebrate his 81st birthday, Francis brings the keen eye of a former journalist and the reflective depth of a life richly lived. His story revisits a childhood moment of misunderstanding between father and son, transformed by time into forgiveness and love. Set against the backdrop of Hong Kong in the 1950s and revisited from his home in Zetland today, Kite and Water Tap speaks to the universal power of empathy and reconciliation. Francis's contribution is a gift to readers and a point of pride for our local community. I warmly congratulate him on this achievement and thank him for his continuing cultural contribution to Heffron.

tree_branches.name: Mr RON HOENIG
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Francis Lee > Mr RON HOENIG

tree_branches.name: Pamela Ang
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Pamela Ang
tree_branches.text: Mr RON HOENIG ( Heffron — Minister for Local Government ) —I congratulate Pamela Ang of Alexandria, whose story "My Brother David" appears in Volume 11 of Seniors' Stories, celebrating the creativity of seniors across NSW. Aged 76, and after a long professional life as an optometrist, Pamela has turned her perceptive lens from eyes to insight, bringing clarity and compassion to her storytelling. Her story captures the enduring bond between brother and sister, tracing their journey from childhood uncertainty to mature friendship and mutual strength. In doing so, she reminds us that family, understanding and humour are anchors through every stage of life. Pamela's work enriches our community's shared narrative and reflects the diverse and compassionate spirit of Alexandria and the wider Heffron electorate. I commend her on this well-deserved recognition and thank her for reminding us of the wisdom that comes from a life fully lived.

tree_branches.name: Mr RON HOENIG
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Pamela Ang > Mr RON HOENIG

tree_branches.name: Marie Tesoriero
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Marie Tesoriero
tree_branches.text: Mr RON HOENIG ( Heffron — Minister for Local Government ) —I congratulate Marie Tesoriero, who has been named the 2025 Fred Hollows Humanitarian of the Year in recognition of her outstanding contribution to people with disability and to children's health. Born with multiple disabilities and having undergone major surgery as a child at Sydney Children's Hospital Randwick, Marie has devoted herself to giving back to others by turning personal adversity into lifelong advocacy. Through her local small business, Made by Cool Marie, she creates and sells handmade art and craft to raise funds for sick children, donating more than $16,000 to the Sydney Children's Hospitals Foundation, with her work now reaching supporters around the world. Marie is also a tireless volunteer for organisations including Meals on Wheels, Guide Dogs Australia, Parkinson's NSW and Northcott, and serves on Bayside Council's Disability Inclusion Action Plan Working Group. A familiar face at local events and festivals, Marie embodies compassion, courage and generosity. I warmly congratulate her on this national recognition and thank her for inspiring all who meet her. Congratulations, Marie!

tree_branches.name: Mr RON HOENIG
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Marie Tesoriero > Mr RON HOENIG

tree_branches.name: Nerrigundah Community Shed
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Nerrigundah Community Shed
tree_branches.text: Dr MICHAEL HOLLAND ( Bega ) —Mr speaker, on Saturday 8 November, I was very pleased to attend the official opening of the brand-new community shed and sports courts at Nerrigundah recreation reserve. This vital space has been built with the support of the Australian Government black summer bushfire recovery grants program. Nerrigundah is situated nineteen kilometres west of Bodalla at the head of the Tuross river valley the 2019 new years eve firestorm destroyed twenty of the twenty-five homes in the village and the community lost Belowra resident and NSW RFS volunteer, col burns. This community shed and sports courts stand as a symbol of resilience, recovery, and the strength of our community. It will serve as a central hub for gatherings, events, and support in times of need — built not only from concrete and steel, but from the spirit of the people it serves. Through the efforts of the community and the Nerrigundah agricultural bureau, the complexities of crown land license and Wagonga local aboriginal land council were successfully resolved. At the opening, the residents stood proudly before a tapestry of a phoenix rising from the ashes like the Nerrigundah community

tree_branches.name: Dr MICHAEL HOLLAND
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Nerrigundah Community Shed > Dr MICHAEL HOLLAND

tree_branches.name: Sergeant Samara Hynes
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Sergeant Samara Hynes
tree_branches.text: Mrs HELEN DALTON ( Murray ) —Mister Speaker, Today I recognise Deniliquin-based Sergeant Samara Hynes of the NSW Police Force for her outstanding commitment to officer safety and wellbeing. At the 2025 Commissioner's Safety Awards held at Goulburn Police Academy, Sergeant Hynes received both the Commissioner's Perpetual Safety Award and the Voluntary Health and Wellbeing Support Role award for her work supporting colleagues beyond her formal duties. In her role at Deniliquin Police Station, Sergeant Hynes manages seized evidence and property and educates officers in safe handling and packaging—from seizure through to storage—with staff safety and wellbeing front of mind. Beyond her formal duties, she supports young officers who relocate to Deniliquin. She is known for her "mum chats", runs fitness/cross fit sessions at her home to support mental and physical health, checks in on staff in her own time, and recently helped a member of the August 2025 class find accommodation and prepare to settle in before graduation. I congratulate Sergeant Hynes on this well-deserved recognition and thank her for the leadership and compassion she provides to the Deniliquin police and wider community.

tree_branches.name: Mrs HELEN DALTON
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Sergeant Samara Hynes > Mrs HELEN DALTON

tree_branches.name: Milton Follies - A Vicar of Dibley Christmas
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Milton Follies - A Vicar of Dibley Christmas
tree_branches.text: Ms LIZA BUTLER ( South Coast ) —Congratulations to the Milton Follies for their latest production, A Vicar of Dibley Christmas, lighting up the stage at the Milton Theatre throughout the month of November. The Milton Follies continues to delight audiences with quality local entertainment, close to home, bringing laughter, creativity, and connection to our community. With more than 20 years of productions behind them, the Milton Follies have built a proud tradition of excellence in the performing arts — a testament to their dedication and community spirit. This year's production combines some of the group's longest-serving members with a wonderful line-up of new talent, both on stage and behind the scenes. Together, they bring the beloved characters from the classic BBC comedy to life in a hilarious and heartwarming Christmas performance. Thank you to the entire cast and crew of the Milton Follies for showcasing local talent and providing such high-quality entertainment for the South Coast. You continue to make our community proud.

tree_branches.name: Ms LIZA BUTLER
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Milton Follies - A Vicar of Dibley Christmas > Ms LIZA BUTLER

tree_branches.name: Home Program
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Home Program
tree_branches.text: Ms LIZA BUTLER ( South Coast ) —I am delighted to recognise and celebrate the inspiring young artists whose work is now shining at the Shoalhaven Regional Gallery in Nowra. The latest exhibition showcases artwork created through the HOME Program, a powerful initiative inviting students from Falls Creek, Greenwell Point, Nowra, Sanctuary Point and Tomerong Public Schools to explore the meaning of 'home'. Over three school terms, these students connected deeply with local Aboriginal artists, community, language and culture. Guided by the talents of Aunty Cheryl Davison, Aunty Deidre Martin and cultural knowledge holder Allen Bloxsome, the students took part in workshops and virtual excursions that enriched their understanding and sparked their creativity. The HOME Program offers young people a meaningful opportunity to engage with First Nations stories, culture and history, building respect, understanding and a stronger connection to the land they call home. The artworks on display reflect this journey with honesty, depth and skill. I extend my heartfelt congratulations to every student artist, to the educators who supported them, and to the First Nations artists and partners who made this program possible. Their collective effort has created an exhibition our community can be proud of.

tree_branches.name: Ms LIZA BUTLER

tree_branches.name: Walcha Coffee Takes Out Top Award
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Walcha Coffee Takes Out Top Award
tree_branches.text: Mr BRENDAN MOYLAN ( Northern Tablelands ) —I recognise Walcha Coffee for their exceptional achievements at the 2025 Business NSW State Awards, where they received both the title of Outstanding Microbusiness and the prestigious honour of Business of the Year. From humble beginnings as a local roaster, Walcha Coffee has grown into a standout example of regional excellence. I congratulate owner Cameron Hayton and his talented team on reaching this remarkable milestone. Their recent success builds on impressive accolades including international medals at the Australasia Golden Bean Awards, where their expertise and consistency have been celebrated among the world's best. I commend Cameron and everyone at Walcha Coffee for their ongoing pursuit of excellence and their contribution to the social and economic life of their hometown. Their success reflects the innovation, teamwork and determination that not only drive their business forward but also enrich and energise the broader Walcha community.

tree_branches.name: Mr BRENDAN MOYLAN

tree_branches.name: Moree Services Football Club 2025 Season
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Moree Services Football Club 2025 Season
tree_branches.text: Mr BRENDAN MOYLAN ( Northern Tablelands ) —I recognise the remarkable achievements of the Moree Services Football Club (FC) throughout an outstanding 2025 season. The club's dedication to nurturing talent across all levels has ensured a bright future for football in Moree. In times when Moree faces many challenges, this celebration of our sporting men and women remind of us all of the strength and joy that comes from community spirit. I congratulate the Moree Services FC Blue team players: Chloe Tindal, Matthew McLane, Steven Pinner, John Addae, Sandeep Basnet, Ethan Hayes, Charles Onus, Todd Jones, Rhys Miller, Adam Ha, Jonah Strahan, Kenneth Wright, Lucas Schembri, Philip Strahan, Travis Hook, PJ Ryan, Dominic Miller and Olivia Pinner on their thrilling grand final victory in the Namoi Football League. Ironically beating last year's winners by the same score! I commend the players, coaches, volunteers, sponsors and loyal supporters whose efforts made this success possible. Your dedication and teamwork, both on and off the field, embody the true spirit of community. The 2025 season will be remembered not only for its triumphs, but for the way the Moree Services FC bought people together through shared effort, pride and love of the game.

tree_branches.name: Mr BRENDAN MOYLAN

tree_branches.name: Matt Dodds – Glen Innes High School
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Matt Dodds – Glen Innes High School
tree_branches.text: Mr BRENDAN MOYLAN ( Northern Tablelands ) —I recognise Matt Dobbs, local teacher at Glen Innes High School on being honoured with the Prime Minister's Prize for Excellence in Science Teaching in Secondary Schools, in the 2025 Prime Minister's Prizes for Science. Such is the importance of this honour, prizes at these awards are considered Australia's most prestigious and highly regarded Science awards. I congratulate Matt on this outstanding and well-deserved accolade, with his excellence recognised for his many achievements, including: inspiring students with his unwavering commitment to science, technology, engineering and mathematics [STEM] education; going beyond to engage students and mentor teachers in his school and nationwide; promoting STEM to students from a range of backgrounds and teaching students from remote communities of NSW. I commend Matt on his creative teaching methods, extra-curricular activities around science, and for continuing to develop and share his knowledge with others. I thank Matt for his dedication to his students and the school community of Glen Innes High School. Matt's valuable contribution to enriching young people's lives in our community is greatly appreciated.

tree_branches.name: Mr BRENDAN MOYLAN

tree_branches.name: Bruce Whiteman, Glenore Brigade
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Bruce Whiteman, Glenore Brigade
tree_branches.text: Mr MARK HODGES ( Castle Hill ) —On Sunday 26 October 2025 I attended The Hills District RFS Awards. I acknowledge Bruce Whiteman who received the Long Service Medal 4th Clasp with a total of 51 years of service. Bruce joined Glenorie Brigade in 1974 in the days of white overalls when the station siren was used to notify of an incident. Bruce became a Crew Leader in 1988 and continues in that role, along with Deputy Captain since 2002. Bruce has assisted in Brigade Driver Training, First Aid Courses and Community Engagement activities. He has been involved in commitments to Gosford, Blue Mountains, Ku-Ring-Gai Chase National Park, Warringah - Pittwater, Hawkesbury—Upper Colo, Newcastle, Sutherland and Gosper's Mountain 2019-20. He actively supports district events holding the honour of district champion or runner-up for 4 NAVEX events in a row and enthusiastically trained younger members in navigation skills to keep Glenorie active in that event. He assisted in logistics and has represented the brigade in Orange Blossom festivals and the Castle Hill Show. Bruce held the role of Brigade President from 2002-2010, and Vice President 2011-2016 and was honoured with Life membership in 2003. He continues to be actively involved in brigade life.

tree_branches.name: Mr MARK HODGES
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Bruce Whiteman, Glenore Brigade > Mr MARK HODGES

tree_branches.name: Christopher Woellner, Round Corner Brigade
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Christopher Woellner, Round Corner Brigade
tree_branches.text: Mr MARK HODGES ( Castle Hill ) —On Sunday 26 October 2025 I attended The Hills District Rural Fire Service Awards. I acknowledge Christopher Woellner who received the National Medal 3rd Clasp with a total of 46 years' service. Christopher joined Round Corner Brigade in March 1979. He built his skills quite quickly including Village Fire, Advanced Fire, Crew Leader, Prescribed Burning Supervisor, First Aid, Rural Fire Driver, and Chainsaw Operator to name a few. Chris has served as Deputy Captain from April 1995 to 2015, and Senior Deputy Captain from 2015 to today. Chris has been actively involved in many Community Education programmes including Winston Hills Oktoberfest, Bunnings BBQ's, Tour De Hills, McHappy Days, Orange Blossom Festival and The Hills Australia Day Emergency Expos. Chris has attended calls to most major fires locally, across NSW and interstate. Chris has also been involved in flood relief and storm damage in Wollongong, Randwick, Nyngan and locally. He has been involved as crew on the majority of 'out of area' commitments by Round Corner for the last 46 years and attends most local after-hours calls. Chris has been involved in shire training as an instructor. Christopher is a worthy recipient of the National Medal.

tree_branches.name: Mr MARK HODGES
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Christopher Woellner, Round Corner Brigade > Mr MARK HODGES

tree_branches.name: Castle Hill & District RSL Sub-Branch, Anzac Ambassadors
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Castle Hill & District RSL Sub-Branch, Anzac Ambassadors
tree_branches.text: Mr MARK HODGES ( Castle Hill ) —Each year the Castle Hill & District RSL Sub-Branch select students to be Anzac Ambassadors. The Ambassadors are taught public speaking, and they research a set subject to present at various commemorations throughout the year. The Castle Hill RSL Sub-Branch Secondary School Ambassador Program began in 2015. The Ambassadors each spoke on Anzac Day at the Anzac Ceremony at Centenary of Anzac Reserve, Castle Hill, Remembrance Day at the Ceremony held on 9 November 2025 at the Balcombe Heights Estate and finally at the Remembrance Day Ceremony held on 11 November 2025 at the Castle Hill RSL Club. This year the Anzac Ambassadors were Ella Dickson (Crestwood High), Harry McMahon (Rouse Hill High), Isaac Browne (Castle Hill High) and Ashlyn Kumar (Oakhill College). I was present at each Ceremony, and I wish to recognise and commend each Ambassador on the respectful manner that each Ambassador brought to the role of Anzac Ambassador. I also acknowledge the Castle Hill & District RSL Club for continuing the Anzac Ambassador Program. I also thank Bryan Mullan and David Hand for their continuing role in the Ambassador Program.

tree_branches.name: Mr MARK HODGES
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Castle Hill & District RSL Sub-Branch, Anzac Ambassadors > Mr MARK HODGES

tree_branches.name: In Memory of Grace Kelly with Thanks to Monique Aboumelhem
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > In Memory of Grace Kelly with Thanks to Monique Aboumelhem
tree_branches.text: Mr JORDAN LANE ( Ryde ) —Ryde faced a tragedy this month involving the heartbreaking loss of Grace Kelly, a beloved mother and part of the St Therese Catholic Primary School community. Grace was known for her kindness and dedication to her family. She leaves behind her husband and 8-year old son. Monique Aboumelhem, a devoted Ryde local, showed extraordinary compassion and leadership during this time. In the days following Grace's passing, Monique brought our community together in the most meaningful way. She coordinated meals for the family, arranged a special birthday gift for Grace's young son Zac, and led a fundraising campaign to help ease the financial pressures on the family. Monique's efforts went far beyond practical support. She became a steady and reassuring presence for a family in crisis and a rallying point for our broader Ryde community to express their empathy and solidarity. Her selfless service is a powerful reminder of the strength and kindness that lives within our neighbourhoods. I thank Monique for her tireless dedication and for exemplifying the community spirit that defines Ryde. Her actions made a real and lasting difference and brought comfort when it was needed most.

tree_branches.name: Mr JORDAN LANE
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > In Memory of Grace Kelly with Thanks to Monique Aboumelhem > Mr JORDAN LANE

tree_branches.name: Remembrance Day Service – Joshua Ong
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Remembrance Day Service – Joshua Ong
tree_branches.text: Mr JORDAN LANE ( Ryde ) —I ask the House to join me in thanking Joshua Ong, a student leader at St Therese's Catholic Primary School, for his meaningful participation in the recent Ryde Remembrance Day service. Joshua delivered a heartfelt prayer for peace. His calm presence and thoughtful delivery reflected the solemnity of the occasion, serving as a powerful reminder of the values we gather to honour on Remembrance Day. These commemorations provide an opportunity to reflect on the sacrifices made by Australian servicemen and women, and to pass on the legacy of remembrance to future generations. Through his contribution, Joshua helped do just that. Having a young local student participate in such a meaningful way demonstrates the strength of our community spirit and the leadership being nurtured in our local schools. I thank Joshua for his poise, compassion and commitment, and I commend him for the example he set on behalf of his school and the broader Ryde community.

tree_branches.name: Remembrance Day Service – Riley Pengilly
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Remembrance Day Service – Riley Pengilly
tree_branches.text: Mr JORDAN LANE ( Ryde ) —I ask the House to join me in thanking Riley Pengilly, School Captain of Epping Boys High School, for his outstanding contribution to the 2025 Ryde Remembrance Day Service. Riley took on the important role of Master of Ceremonies at this year's commemoration, which brought together veterans, families, and local community members to honour those who served and sacrificed in defence of our nation. As MC, Riley demonstrated poise, leadership and respect beyond his years. His role was pivotal in setting the tone for what was a solemn, reflective and dignified ceremony. I commend Riley for the maturity and presence he brought to this occasion. Remembrance Day holds deep meaning for many in our community, particularly for the families of our veterans. It was heartening to see a young leader like Riley rise to the occasion with such care and thoughtfulness. His contribution reflected a broader spirit of respect and civic pride among our youth, which is encouraging to witness. I thank Riley once again for his efforts and commend Epping Boys High School for continuing to instill a strong sense of service and responsibility in its students.
