tree_branches.name: Penrith War History Museum
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Penrith War History Museum
tree_branches.text: Ms KAREN McKEO WN ( Penrith ) —The Penrith RSL has recently completed renovations, which included the creation of an Australian Military Museum dedicated to preserving and honouring our nation's military history. This museum is a remarkable tribute, showcasing authentic uniforms, medals, weapons, and other artefacts from Australian soldiers' conflicts. It is filled with memorabilia and stories that bring our history to life. The Penrith RSL generously built and provided the museum to the local sub-branch at no cost, with the purpose of re-establishing a space where military history and treasured memorabilia can be shared with the community. The spirit of ANZAC Day and Remembrance Day is deeply embedded in this initiative, reminding us of the sacrifice, struggle, and immense toll of war—and why we must always honour those who gave their lives for our home and values. A heartfelt thank you goes to Anthony Eddie, President of the Penrith RSL Sub-Branch, and the Penrith RSL for making this vision a reality. We also extend our gratitude to all the volunteers, donors, and individuals who contributed equipment, memorabilia, and personal stories to enrich the museum experience. Your efforts ensure that the legacy of service and sacrifice will never be forgotten.

tree_branches.name: Ms KAREN McKEOWN

tree_branches.name: Relay for Life Penrith
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Relay for Life Penrith
tree_branches.text: Ms KAREN McKEOWN ( Penrith ) —I thank the organisers and participants of Relay for Life Penrith 2025. The annual Relay took place in September and set an ambitious fundraising target of $80,000. Thanks to the generosity and dedication of the community, organisers, volunteers and relayers, the event raised more than $95,000, surpassing the goal and making a real difference for those affected by cancer. The relay featured 382 participants across 40 teams who took part in a moving 12 hour program of walking, remembrance and celebration. Funds raised support Cancer Council's vital work in research, prevention and patient support, helping to drive discoveries, deliver services and reduce the burden of cancer in our community. I want to recognise the tireless efforts of Cancer Council staff, the many volunteers who organised logistics, marshalled activities and provided care, and every individual who gave their time, energy and donations. Your compassion and commitment demonstrate the strength of Penrith when we come together for a common cause, a future free from cancer.

tree_branches.name: Ms KAREN McKEOWN
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Relay for Life Penrith > Ms KAREN McKEOWN

tree_branches.name: Saving True Blues
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Saving True Blues
tree_branches.text: Ms KAREN McKEOWN ( Penrith ) —Congratulations to Lucinda Harvey, the founder and driving force behind Saving True Blues Charity on a successful fundraising event recently held at Penrith Paceway. Lucinda's commitment to mental health awareness, community engagement, and advocacy demonstrates her outstanding leadership. Lucinda founded 'Saving True Blues' to raise awareness for suicide and mental health. What began as a local initiative has now expanded into a state-wide movement. Lucinda's innovative approach involves organising 4-wheel-driving and camping weekends, providing a platform for individuals to step out of their comfort zones, explore nature, and engage in crucial conversations about mental health. We know that mental health is one of the most important challenges facing our community today. Behind every statistic is a person: a mate, a partner, a son or daughter, a colleague, or a neighbour. And far too often, those who are struggling the most feel like they have to do it alone. That's why initiatives like Saving True Blues are so important. They remind us that strength isn't about silence. It's about reaching out and showing up for one another. It's about creating spaces where people feel seen, heard, and supported. What matters is that those conversations happen. Penrith is proud.

tree_branches.name: Ms KAREN McKEOWN

tree_branches.name: Samson Alogwu
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Samson Alogwu
tree_branches.text: Ms STEPHANIE DI PASQUA ( Drummoyne ) —I rise to acknowledge Mr Samson Alogwu, a bright high school student from Regents Park Christian School, who recently joined me in the NSW Parliament as the Member for Drummoyne for a Day. It was a pleasure to host Samson and his mother Karen for a tour of the Parliament and to watch Question Time in the Bear Pit. Samson is an outstanding public speaker and a passionate young leader. At just 15 years old, he has already taken part in the Global Round of the World Scholar Cup in Christchurch and recently visited Yale to compete in the Tournament of Champions International Debating Competition. He received three gold and two bronze medals at the Competition. I sincerely thank Samson for taking the time to visit the Parliament. We spoke about the importance of inclusion in education and opportunities for young people. I know the future is in safe hands with young people like him and I wish him all the very best, particularly as he continues to excel in public speaking.

tree_branches.name: Ms STEPHANIE DI PASQUA

tree_branches.name: Dr Uma Srinivasan
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Dr Uma Srinivasan
tree_branches.text: Ms STEPHANIE DI PASQUA ( Drummoyne ) —I rise to acknowledge a local Rhodes resident and author, Dr Uma Srinivasan and to sincerely congratulate her on the launch of her new book 'Etched in Gold'. Etched in Gold is a historical fiction, telling the story of two Indian women connected through their passion for music and their culture throughout the 16th to 18th centuries. The novel is an important reminder of the power of storytelling in sharing histories and preserving cultural heritage. Prior to beginning her journey as an author, Dr Srinivasan worked as a computer scientist, obtaining her PhD from the University of New South Wales. Her transition to literature is a testament to her talent and dedication to lifelong learning. I have known Dr Srinivasan for a number of years during her time serving on the City of Canada Bay Council's Rhodes Community Committee, where she volunteered her time serving Rhodes and working to bring better services for the community. I sincerely congratulate Dr Srinivasan on the release of her novel 'Etched in Gold' and I wish her all the very best.

tree_branches.name: Hills Football Association
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Hills Football Association
tree_branches.text: Mr RAY WILLIAMS ( Kellyville ) —I'm pleased to recognise the 10-year anniversary of the Hills Football Association, an organisation whose roots were laid well before its 2015 formation and 2016 launch. A dedicated local association became necessary when thousands of Hills players were travelling over 30 kilometres away each Saturday, instead of within their own community. Today, over 16,000 players take part in Hills Football competitions close to home. First formed as the Sydney Hills Football Association, it launched with more than 8,000 registered players. The founding clubs included Baulkham Hills FC, Castle Hill RSL Rockets, Castle Hill United, Hills Grammar, Hills Knights, Kellyville United, North Rocks Soccer Club, North West FC, Norwest Cougars and Rouse Hill Rangers. Renamed the Hills Football Association, its inaugural committee Graeme Luck, Matthew Perram, Craig Gough, Suzan Torville, Dino DiGulio, William Renton and Mick Pawelko worked tirelessly to shape the strong organisation we see today, now home to over twice the original number of clubs and players. Next year, Hills Football will become a formalised "Association Zone'' under Football NSW after nine years as an affiliate. I thank all who supported its growth, including the Hills Shire Council and former GM Dave Walker.

tree_branches.name: Ariana Mckechnie
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Ariana Mckechnie
tree_branches.text: Ms ELENI PE TINOS ( Miranda ) —I recognise Ariana McKechnie, whose book The Rainbow Boy has been published by Xlibris, marking an impressive milestone for the young writer from Menai High School. Ariana first wrote The Rainbow Boy at just eight years of age during the COVID-19 lockdowns, choosing to use that challenging period as an opportunity for creativity and expression. Her story reflects a strong interest in reading, storytelling and imaginative writing—interests that continue to guide her learning, particularly in English and literacy. The Rainbow Boy follows the journey of a young boy who lives among the clouds with his family, whose special role is to create rainbows. After accidentally falling to Earth and becoming separated from both his family and his colours, he begins a journey of rediscovery. With the help of a girl he meets in this unfamiliar world, he navigates emotional challenges and new experiences in search of identity, belonging and connection. Ariana's initiative and creativity at such a young age are commendable. Her published work stands as a testament to the imagination, resilience and determination shown by many young people during that difficult time.

tree_branches.name: Ms ELENI PETINOS

tree_branches.name: Jannali East Public School's Remembrance Day
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Jannali East Public School's Remembrance Day
tree_branches.text: Ms ELENI PETINOS ( Miranda ) —I recognise Jannali East Public School for their thoughtful and engaging commemoration of Remembrance Day. At the 11th hour on the 11th day of the 11th month, Australians pause to honour the soldiers who gave their lives in service of our nation. This year, Jannali East Public School marked the occasion with Kokoda: Footsteps of the Brave - a powerful film created by Year 5 and 6 students with guidance from Australian Army Warrant Officer Class 2 Jeremy Lowe. Drawing on the recollections of veteran Reg Chard OAM and the students' moving reenactments, the film brought the Kokoda Trail to life for their school community. I acknowledge the talented students behind the film, namely Nathaniel Bao, Sebastian Burke, Chad Graham, Eva Green, Violet Parker, Ned Rossman, Delilah Thorburn and Brooklynn Vanzanten for their exceptional creativity and dedication. I also thank Assistant Principal Michelle Love and Jeremy Lowe for their leadership in teaching students about the sacrifices of our troops, supported by Lieutenant-Colonel Conrad Walsh and Warren Crotty. Through Kokoda: Footsteps of the Brave we are reminded that remembrance is the bridge between the courage of the past and the gratitude of the present.

tree_branches.name: Ms ELENI PETINOS

tree_branches.name: Miranda RSL Sub-Branch's 90th Anniversary
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Miranda RSL Sub-Branch's 90th Anniversary
tree_branches.text: Ms ELENI PETINOS ( Miranda ) —I celebrate 90 remarkable years of the Miranda RSL Sub-Branch and its enduring service to our community. In 1935, returned servicemen Bill Luxton and Alex Porter recognised the need for a place where veterans could reconnect with those who understood their experiences. Their call for a meeting at the Miranda School of Arts led to the formation of the Miranda Sub-Branch - a place that nurtured camaraderie through some of Australia's most challenging decades. From its humble beginnings, the Sub-Branch grew into a supportive home offering welfare assistance, social connection, and a library dedicated to preserving military history. Today, it proudly marks nine decades of honouring service, supporting veterans, and strengthening community ties. To commemorate this extraordinary milestone, the Miranda RSL Sub-Branch hosted a 90th anniversary luncheon on 9 November, bringing together ex-servicemen, families, and friends to share stories, memories, and fellowship. I recognise Steve Bull, Joanne Beavis, Warren Barnes OAM, Alan Lark, Reverend Jennie Everist, Greg Beavis, Shane Hall, Jim Lowe and Bruce Grill for their contributions to this special occasion. Ninety years on, the Miranda RSL Sub-Branch stands as a testament to resilience, mateship and unwavering commitment to our veterans.

tree_branches.name: Ms ELENI PETINOS

tree_branches.name: Happy Diwali

tree_branches.text: Ms DONNA DAVIS ( Parramatta ) —It is a privilege to represent the incredibly diverse constituency of Parramatta that is also home to the second largest Indian community in New South Wales. Parramatta is home to thriving small and medium businesses, many operated by our incredibly innovative Indian businesspeople across the entire electorate. During the Festival of Lights celebrations, the Premier and I met with several business owners and community service providers in Little India and Harris Park. Special acknowledgement goes to Suchitra Jotsinghani of Cincotta Chemist, Jyoti Prakash of Chilli Bates, Ashish Batel of India Bazaar and Vandana and Nitin Setia of Ginger Indian Restaurant. In the season of Diwali, it was a pleasure to invite the Premier to the Parramatta electorate to witness quintessential Indian Australian success stories. Hardworking small business owners who enrich the fabric of our community and form the centrepiece of our society. As we celebrate the Festival of Lights, I cannot think of any other symbolism more appropriate than recognising some of the leading lights of our Indian-Australian diaspora. I wish a Happy Diwali to all those who celebrate.

From powerful vocals to soulful solos, and mesmerising cultural dance performances, the staff of the Western Sydney Local Health District showed that their talents go far beyond healthcare – they truly know how to shine on stage! It is inspiring to see workplaces celebrating hidden talents, teamwork and cultural diversity, all while giving back to the very wards and teams that make our health system so strong. I also want to give a huge shout-out to Parramatta, my vibrant electorate, because events like this prove that community and heart thrive in our workplaces for the benefit of many.

tree_branches.name: Foundation Day 2025
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Foundation Day 2025
tree_branches.text: Ms DONNA DAVIS ( Parramatta ) —I was delighted to join the community on Saturday 1st November for Foundation Day, celebrating Parramatta's proud history and heritage. This year Foundation Day was held at Hambledon Cottage, providing an opportunity to introduce this State heritage listed site to a wider audience as families, friends and even a few four-legged locals enjoyed the free family event. Foundation Day marks the arrival of Governor Arthur Phillip in Parramatta on 2 November 1788 and the start of agricultural projects in the area. The date has traditionally been celebrated with large civic events, street carnivals and parades. In more recent years the actual day has become less of a focus than the sharing of Parramatta's heritage and stories. This year visitors enjoyed guided tours of Hambledon Cottage, horse drawn carriage rides, weaving and blacksmith demonstrations, roving entertainment, children's workshops, face painting an animal farm and entertainment from the Parramatta's City Band. Congratulations to the Parramatta and Districts Historical Society, the City of Parramatta, the Parramatta Lions Club and all who were involved in making the day a success.

tree_branches.name: Ms DONNA DAVIS

tree_branches.name: Gennaro Abignano
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Gennaro Abignano
tree_branches.text: Ms KOBI SHETTY ( Balmain ) —Today I honour the life of Gennaro Alfonso Abignano AM, who passed away on 24 October 2025 aged 93. Gennaro devoted his life to family, his friends, and his community. Gennaro was the beloved husband of Maria and a devoted father and father-in-law to Nina and Alan, Luisa and Tony, Biagio and Sharon, Joseph and Clair, Mario and Marilena, and Pierre and Sophie. He was a proud Nonno to sixteen grandchildren and fourteen great-grandchildren. His family was his greatest pride. A highly respected figure in the Italian-Australian community, had a successful career in construction and was one of the founding members and later President of the Associazione Napoletana, an organisation dedicated to preserving and sharing the language, heritage, and traditions of Italy. Through his leadership, he helped build a strong and enduring cultural community, enriching the lives of generations of families and bringing joy and friendship to all members. Gennaro Abignano AM leaves behind a legacy of service, generosity, and cultural pride. I extend my deepest condolences to his family, his many friends, and to all who were touched by his remarkable life.

tree_branches.name: Ms KOBI SHETTY
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Gennaro Abignano > Ms KOBI SHETTY

tree_branches.name: Associazione Napoletana
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Associazione Napoletana
tree_branches.text: Ms KOBI SHETTY ( Balmain ) —I would like to recognise the Associazione Napoletana, a vibrant community of local Italians, who come together each month to share their love of food, culture, and friendship. These monthly gatherings celebrate not only the rich culinary traditions of Naples and southern Italy, but also the warmth and generosity of a community that welcomes everyone to enjoy great company and great food. Italian culture is woven into the heart of Leichhardt, shaping the character of our community, strengthening and enriching the lives of community members and visitors alike. I had the pleasure of attending this month's dinner and got to experience the delight this organisation brings to the community. Thank you to the President Michele Fezza and his wife Susanna Fezza, Vice President Carmine Charley Telese, Director Carmine Zarrella, Secartary Franca De Francesco, Treasurer Salvatore Rizzo, Giovanna Cardamone, the executive director of Italian welfare group ItSoWel in Wollongong, Luisa Perugini and all those involved in Associazione Napoletana for fostering friendship, community and tradition in Leichhardt, and thank you for having me at this month's dinner, it was an absolute delight.

tree_branches.name: Ms KOBI SHETTY

tree_branches.name: YAN Cai
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > YAN Cai
tree_branches.text: Mr PHILIP DONATO ( Orange ) —Mr Speaker, I rise to acknowledge the outstanding contribution of Yan Cai, a long-standing and deeply respected member of the Orange community for more than three decades. Yan is known for her generosity of spirit and her commitment to helping others feel welcome and included. She plays an active role in the multicultural sewing group and conversational English classes for new migrants, offering encouragement, friendship and practical support to people adjusting to life in a new country. Her ability to connect with individuals from diverse backgrounds has created a sense of belonging for many who might otherwise feel isolated. Yan's involvement in community events such as Harmony Day and local multicultural celebrations has helped build understanding, cultural exchange and positive relationships across the region. She consistently shows up where support is needed—listening, helping, translating, teaching skills and strengthening social participation. Her dedication to community development extends to her own growth, undertaking further study to better contribute to local programs and increase her capacity to support others. Yan's contribution is not loud or self-promoting. It is steady, genuine and deeply impactful. She makes our community more welcoming, more compassionate and more connected.

tree_branches.name: Mr PHILIP DONATO
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > YAN Cai > Mr PHILIP DONATO

tree_branches.name: Bev Williams
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Bev Williams
tree_branches.text: Mr PHILIP DONATO ( Orange ) —Mr Speaker, I acknowledge the outstanding contribution of Bev Williams, whose decades of quiet, determined service have strengthened the wellbeing, dignity and social cohesion of our community. Bev has been involved in community support work for many years, offering her time, compassion and leadership to organisations that assist people experiencing financial hardship, homelessness and social isolation. Her long association with FoodCare Orange has been particularly impactful. Bev has served in both leadership and volunteer coordination roles, helping ensure that individuals and families in need have access to affordable and nutritious food in a respectful and welcoming environment. Her commitment to preserving dignity in the support process has been central to FoodCare's positive reputation. Bev has also contributed to a range of local organisations, including PCYC, Lifeline, St Vincent de Paul, and programs that support multicultural families and newly arrived migrants. She works collaboratively, listens deeply, and always seeks practical, meaningful ways to support others. Her service reflects a genuine belief that strong communities are built through compassion, shared effort and respect. Bev leads not from recognition, but from care — and our region is stronger because of her. I commend Bev Williams for her steadfast dedication to Orange.

tree_branches.name: Mr PHILIP DONATO
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Bev Williams > Mr PHILIP DONATO

tree_branches.name: David Farrell
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > David Farrell
tree_branches.text: Mr PHILIP DONATO ( Orange ) —David Farrell aged 83 from my electorate, is a man who embodies the true spirit of small country communities. Mr Farrell was recently recognised for his extraordinary commitment to his community through his involvement with the Cudal-Cargo Lions Club for more than 40 years. He was awarded the prestigious Melvin Jones Fellowship as an acknowledgement of more than four decades of his service to the community through a number of projects to enhance the quality of life of district residents. During his years of service to the club, Mr Farrell has held every executive role from president, to secretary and treasurer and only recently decided to step back from the role of treasurer at the club. He is a valued member of the community who first came the town as a Postmaster 40 years ago and became immediately invested in giving back by becoming involved in the process of the inaugural committee for the formation of the Cudal-Cargo Lions Club. During his time of service to the club, Mr Farrell has over seen the donation of $50,000 to Cancer Care Western NSW as well as a strong involvement with the formation of the Cudal and Cargo Men's Sheds.

tree_branches.name: Mr PHILIP DONATO

tree_branches.name: Recognition of Collin Hollis
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Recognition of Collin Hollis
tree_branches.text: Ms KATELIN McINERNEY ( Kiama ) —I wish to recognise Collin Hollis for his outstanding contribution to horticulture, community life, and public service, and to congratulate him on being awarded the President's Award by the Garden Clubs of Australia. This honour reflects a lifetime of dedication to growing communities as much as gardens. Collin has been a generous leader in the gardening world, sharing his knowledge, enthusiasm, and mentorship with countless gardeners across New South Wales. His work with local garden clubs, community gardens, and public beautification projects has helped enrich shared spaces, foster social connection, and encourage the joy of growing. Collin has also played a significant role in strengthening horticultural organisations, supporting education, workshops, and opportunities for people of all ages to engage with gardening. Beyond his horticultural leadership, Collin has contributed to public life through his service in Parliament and ongoing community advocacy, always guided by a belief in service, care, and strengthening local communities. He has left a lasting mark on public spaces, community organisations, and I thank and congratulate Collin on this well-deserved honour and for his longstanding and ongoing contribution to the community.

tree_branches.name: Ms KATELIN McINERNEY
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Recognition of Collin Hollis > Ms KATELIN McINERNEY

tree_branches.name: RFS Captain Hanna Mcinerney
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > RFS Captain Hanna Mcinerney
tree_branches.text: Ms KATELIN McINERNEY ( Kiama ) —I today recognise Captain Hannah McInerney, who was selected as the 2025 Illawarra Regional Adult Volunteer of the Year for her outstanding leadership and commitment to the community. As Captain of the Jamberoo Rural Fire Service, Hannah has devoted more than 15 years to protecting lives and property. She made history as the first female brigade captain in the Illawarra and continues to lead her team with professionalism, empathy, and courage. Under her leadership, women now hold most officer positions in the brigade, reflecting her strong focus on inclusion and mentorship. Beyond her firefighting responsibilities, Hannah delivers fire safety programs in local preschools, supports community recovery during severe weather events, and volunteers with the Kiama Surf Life Saving Club. Hannah's recognition as Regional Adult Volunteer of the Year is a fitting acknowledgment of her exceptional service and dedication to others. Her leadership and compassion embody the true spirit of volunteerism, and she continues to inspire those around her to serve their community with pride and purpose.

tree_branches.name: Ms KATELIN McINERNEY
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > RFS Captain Hanna Mcinerney > Ms KATELIN McINERNEY

tree_branches.name: Recognition of Mark Burns
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Recognition of Mark Burns
tree_branches.text: Ms KATELIN McINERNEY ( Ki ama ) —I would like to recognise Mark Burns, the founder of The Man Walk, for his outstanding contribution to men's health and wellbeing in our community and across Australia. Beginning in Kiama in 2019, Mark launched a simple idea with powerful intent: to create a space where men could walk, talk, and support one another without judgement. Since then, The Man Walk has grown to over 80 locations nationwide, with more than 130,000 men taking part. Through Mark's leadership, thousands of men have found connection, routine, mateship, and a safe place to speak openly about the challenges they face. Countless participants credit The Man Walk with improving their mental health, building lasting friendships, and, in some cases, changing or even saving lives. Mark's vision has sparked a movement rooted in compassion and community strength. We thank him for walking alongside so many and for inspiring a culture of reaching out for support.

tree_branches.name: Ms KATELIN McINERNEY

tree_branches.name: Kumon Epping Education Centre
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Kumon Epping Education Centre
tree_branches.text: Ms MONICA TUDEHOPE ( Epping ) —I ask the Parliament to join me in Congratulating the Kumon Epping Education Centre on their great achievements over the year. With Jarrod Dong at the helm of the centre, over 100 students now attend and show remarkable results. Six of these students made it into the National Top 20 list in Kumon Australia and I would particularly like to Individually congratulate them for their outstanding achievements: Raymond C in Math and English in Kindy, Amy D- Math and English in Year 2, Triti B- English Year 3, Vedansh- Math Yr 6, Nivaan G- Math Year 6 and Lucas B Math for Year 5. These bright children should be very proud of their achievement, and I wish them continued success in their future endeavours. This success is a testament not only to the talent and hard work of the students, but also to the teachers who supported them. Congratulations on a wonderful end to the academic yar of 2025 I look forward to seeing their future achievements and celebrating the continued success of Kumon Epping Education Centre.

tree_branches.name: Emily Wong
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Emily Wong
tree_branches.text: Ms MONICA TUDEHOPE ( Epping ) —I ask the Parliament to join with me in acknowledging the dedication of amazing volunteers that live in the Epping electorate. One such person is Emily Wong who has been a volunteer for many years across several organisations. I would like to highlight some of those contributions to provide a sense of her dedication to her community. Emilly has served as the Mini Coordinator Registrar at the Epping Football Club. For Carlingford Public School, she has worked in the canteen and served in the roles of P&C Vice President, P&C Uniform Shop Coordinator, P&C Class Parent Coordinator, P&C Fundraising Coordinator and P&C President. She has also served on the North Rocks Carlingford Little Athletics Committee. I met Emily when she was coordinating the first Carlingford Public School fete, even though her children no longer attended the school! Emily's contribution to our community across sporting clubs and school groups demonstrates that there are people in our community that go above and beyond to serve. This makes our community stronger and I am proud to have Emily as part of my community and to be able to make a small recognition of her contributions. Thank you Emily.

tree_branches.name: Zonta Club of Hunter Newcastle Inc.
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Zonta Club of Hunter Newcastle Inc.
tree_branches.text: Mr TIM CRAKANTHORP ( Newcastle ) —Tonight, I would like to celebrate the wonderful Zonta Club of Hunter Newcastle Inc (Zonta Club) -a group of extraordinary people who turn compassion into action and hope into real changes. Zonta Club has beautifully created gorgeous community initiatives such as Refuge Support which recently helped six local women's refuges; Breast Cushions which amplifies Hunter Breast Cancer Foundation's efforts and provides sewed breast cushions and drainage bags for patients at their local hospital following breast surgery. Since 2015, their Birthing Kits initiative has successfully delivered 7,800 kits which are clean and sent to pregnant women in rural or low resources internationally. One of my favourite ones is Zonta says NO to Violence Against Women, a fabulous campaign that raises awareness through various activities and supportive projects during the 16 Days of Activism in the Newcastle and Hunter area. Moreover, Zonta Club is also well known for their generous Scholarship and Award programs including Women in Technology, Achievement Award for a Young Indigenous Woman, Young Women in Public Affairs and so much more. Thank you, Zonta, for showing us what's possible when kindness leads, and action follow.

tree_branches.name: Brain Industries
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Brain Industries
tree_branches.text: Mr TIM CRAKANTHORP ( Newcastle ) —Congratulations to Brain Industries, a Carrington-based manufacturing group that won Manufacturer of the Year (under 50 employees) at the 2025 Hunter Manufacturing Awards. Brain Industries specialises in manufacture customised equipment for operations in the mining, tunnelling, transport, and agriculture industries. Their products are Australian designed and built, ensuring that equipment is built to local conditions. Brain Industries have also expanded to deliver industrial equipment around the world Newcastle and the Hunter has a long history as a manufacturing hub of NSW and Australia. The Hunter Manufacturing Awards was established to recognise the hard work and innovation of local businesses. Brain Industries was recognised for their strong export performance, innovation, workforce engagement. I congratulate the whole team on this well-deserved achievement.

tree_branches.name: Mr TIM CRAKANTHORP
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Brain Industries > Mr TIM CRAKANTHORP

tree_branches.name: Varley Group - Hma Hall of Fame
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Varley Group - Hma Hall of Fame
tree_branches.text: Mr TIM CRAKANTHORP ( Newcastle ) —Congratulations to Varley Group on its induction into the Hunter Manufacturing Awards Hall of Fame. This achievement recognises nearly 140 years of innovation and craftsmanship in the Hunter region. Founded in 1886, Varley is one of Newcastle's oldest and most respected companies, a large local employer, and national leader across the defence, emergency services, marine, health, cyber, and mining sectors. This honour celebrates Varley's remarkable ability to evolve and diversify while keeping its headquarters and heart firmly in the Hunter. The company's commitment to apprenticeships, veterans' employment, and STEM education, through partnerships with local schools, TAFE NSW, and the University of Newcastle, continues to shape the next generation of manufacturing talent. Employing more than 1,200 people across 12 facilities, Varley's impact extends well beyond its projects. It stands as a symbol of Hunter ingenuity, adaptability, and pride in building things that matter. Congratulations to the entire Varley team on this prestigious recognition and for continuing to define what world-class manufacturing looks like, in Newcastle and right across the Hunter.

tree_branches.name: Retirement of Chief Inspector Guy Guiana
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Retirement of Chief Inspector Guy Guiana
tree_branches.text: Mr DAVID LAYZELL ( Upper Hunter ) —Hunter Valley Police District has today farewelled Chief Inspector Guy Guiana marking the completion of his 38-year career with the NSW Police Force. Chief Inspector Guiana trained at the Goulburn Police Academy in the late-1980s. His service in the NSW Police Force has included General Duties, Detectives, Anti-Theft Squad and Police Airwing crewman. His rise through the ranks saw Guy promoted to Inspector beginning more than 20-years of service in the Upper Hunter. Inspector Guiana was further promoted to the rank of Chief Inspector and decorated with the Australian Police Medal awarded in the Australia Day 2013 Honours List. Chief Inspector Guiana's final day of service has been acknowledged with a ceremonial farewell at Muswellbrook Police Station, where he was 'marched' out to the sound of bagpipes. Thank you, Guy, for your contribution to New South Wales and the communities of the Hunter Valley, especially the Upper Hunter. Congratulation on your policing career and enjoy your retirement from the 'beat'.

tree_branches.name: Mr DAVID LAYZELL

tree_branches.name: Upper Hunter Learner Night Drive
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Upper Hunter Learner Night Drive
tree_branches.text: Mr DAVID LAYZELL ( Upper Hunter ) —I want to acknowledge the ongoing work in the Upper Hunter to improve road safety starting with our newest road users. Upper Hunter Shire Council and Hunter Valley Police District began the Learner Night Driver Program in late-2024 and it is being strongly supported by the community. Hunter Learner Night Drive is for learner drivers of any age, who must be accompanied by an appropriately licenced supervisor aged over 25. The event exposes learner drivers to real life driving scenarios and the opportunity to interact with police in a controlled environment. Learner drivers use a track at Scone Airport and get to experience stationary and mobile breath tests with police as well as receiving advice and guidance on how to safely undertake these tasks. The track includes a section where drivers can practice reverse parallel parking, roadcraft and vehicle manoeuvring. Learner Night Drive is supported by Hunter Valley Highway Patrol, Transport for NSW, NSW Ambulance, Singleton Council, Muswellbrook Shire Council and Merriwa VRA. I also want to acknowledge the corporate supporters assisting this initiative including JBS Scone, Bengalla Mining Company, Pays Air Service and Hunter Warbirds.

Seniors' Stories is an annual collection of 100 short stories written by NSW Seniors Card holders statewide. tree_branches.name: Pauline Menzcer Statue Unveiling
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Pauline Menzcer Statue Unveiling
tree_branches.text: Ms KELLIE SLOANE ( Vaucluse ) —I would like to celebrate the unveiling of the Pauline Menzcer Statue at South Bondi. From humble beginnings at Bondi, Pauline became our very own ASP world champion. Along the way she became known for her refined surfing style, valiant big wave approach and hilarious antics at post contest parties. She was, after all, known by friends as "naughty Pauls". Pauline's story – including her ability to overcome personal adversity – and significant health issues – were detailed in the movie "Girls Can't Surf". And it was the Director of that movie- Chris Nelius - who has been the driving force behind the statue –from concept to permissions and funding. Chris points out that only 6% of statues in this country are of women. There are more statues of animals. So now there's one more – to honour Pauline's legacy and inspire the next generation of young women and men to follow their dreams.

tree_branches.name: Ms KELLIE SLOANE

tree_branches.name: Peter Burton
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Peter Burton
tree_branches.text: Ms LIESL TESCH ( Gosford ) —It is a pleasure to congratulate Peter Burton on being named as a recipient of the Gosford Community Champion Award. Peter has shown outstanding dedication through his instrumental work in nurturing and supporting the Senior's Friendship Club. He has invested significant time and energy into addressing challenges and providing consistent support to ensure the club remains a vibrant and welcoming space. The Senior's Friendship Club plays a vital role in the lives of its members, encouraging social connection, new experiences, and lasting friendships. By creating opportunities for seniors to engage with others and participate in community activities, the club helps reduce isolation, depression and poor health, issues that can deeply affect older members of our community. Peter's tireless efforts to sustain and grow this important organisation are a true testament to his community spirit. His unwavering commitment has ensured that the club not only remains open but continues to thrive as a source of connection and belonging for so many. Thank you, Peter, for your exceptional contribution to bringing our community together and for the positive impact you continue to make.

tree_branches.name: Maitland Regional Art Gallery Celebrates 50 Years
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Maitland Regional Art Gallery Celebrates 50 Years
tree_branches.text: Ms JENNY AITCHISON ( Maitland — Minister for Regional Transport, and Minister for Roads ) —Congratulations to Maitland Regional Art Gallery (MRAG), which this month celebrates 50 years since opening its doors. I'm extremely proud of what the gallery has achieved in the half-century it has served the public. In this time, the gallery has proven to be a much-loved institution not only in the local community but across the state and nation. Maitland Regional Art Gallery has showcased the works of many celebrated artists from across the local community, the Hunter region and Australia. The feedback from those who have visited over the years is testament to its vital role as a cultural hub and its critical importance to the health, wellbeing and vibrancy of our community. The gallery's history stretches back to April 1975, when the Maitland City Art Gallery, as it was then known, was established on Church Street, Maitland. The art gallery relocated to its current home on Maitland's High Street in 2003. Congratulations MRAG on this milestone and for your contribution to the Maitland community.

tree_branches.name: Ms JENNY AITCHISON
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Maitland Regional Art Gallery Celebrates 50 Years > Ms JENNY AITCHISON

tree_branches.name: Trish Sullivan
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Trish Sullivan
tree_branches.text: Ms JENNY AITCHISON ( Maitland — Minister for Regional Transport, and Minister for Roads ) —Congratulations to Trish Sullivan for an incredible 20 years of dedicated service as a School Learning Support Officer with the Department of Education. Trish's commitment to supporting students' learning and wellbeing has made a lasting and positive impact on every school community she has been part of. For the past seven years at Metford Public School, Trish has been a valued and much-loved member of the community. Her compassion, patience, and steady support for students needing additional assistance have earned her deep respect from students, staff, and families alike. Trish is retiring in preparation to relocate to the Northern Territory, this new chapter brings the wonderful opportunity for Trish to be closer to her family and to enjoy precious time with her first grandchild, an exciting and joyful milestone. Warmest thanks are extended for Trish's remarkable service, her kindness, and the unwavering dedication she has shown throughout her career. Trish will be greatly missed at Metford Public School, and very best wishes as she begins this next adventure.

tree_branches.name: Ms JENNY AITCHISON

tree_branches.name: Vale Daniel William Austin, OAM
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Vale Daniel William Austin, OAM
tree_branches.text: Ms JENNY AITCHISON ( Maitland — Minister for Regional Transport, and Minister for Roads ) —Mr Austin was a respected leader and quintessential gentleman - a pillar of the Maitland community, where his wisdom and wit shaped headlines and lives for decades. Born in Singleton, his early years were shaped by resilience. Mr Austin attended Francis Xavier Catholic Primary School and Singleton High School. His formal education was cut short at age 14, despite winning a scholarship to Marist Brothers Maitland. At 20, Mr Austin made a bold career switch, leaving a secure railway job to become a journalist, hired as a B-grade journalist at the Singleton Argus. His dedication was legendary: to master his craft, he learnt shorthand, and famously read a dictionary from A-Z, devoured a Roget's Thesaurus, and systematically worked his way through a 20-volume encyclopedia, all to build his vocabulary and general knowledge. Mr Austin worked at the Singleton Argus, founded the Cessnock Advertiser, moved to the The Mercury, The Manning River Times, returning to be Editor of The Maitland Mercury, ultimately serving as the managing editor-in-chief for Rural Press, overseeing approximately 180 country newspapers across Australia. VALE Mr Austin and thank you for your service to so many communities.

tree_branches.name: Ms JENNY AITCHISON

tree_branches.name: 2025 Excellence In Early Childhood Education Awards
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > 2025 Excellence In Early Childhood Education Awards
tree_branches.text: Mr MATT CROSS ( Davidson ) —On 8 November, I attended the 2025 Excellence in Early Childhood Education Awards. This is the largest annual celebration of the early childhood education and care sector in New South Wales. The evening brought together over 600 educators, teachers, service providers, support staff, families and friends to recognise the outstanding contribution that early learning professionals make to children aged 0-5. Early childhood services play a vital role in supporting families, strengthening communities and giving young children the best possible start in life. I recognise two winners who provide services for the Davidson electorate. Congratulations to Bindook Cottage Terrey Hills, winner of the Metropolitan Services Excellence Award for Small Private Metropolitan Service; and Monalisa Jani, Teaching Director at CASS Gumnut Early Learning Centre in St Leonards NSW for Director/Nominated Supervisor Excellence Award. I recognise the NSW executive committee for their leadership, President Lyn Connolly, Vice President Nicole Upfold, Treasurer Mark Wharton, Secretary Eleni Wilson, and Members Donus Demir, Renae Donovan, Rita Totino, Diane Saba, Nate Wang and the Chief Executive Officer of Australian Childcare Alliance Chiang Lim for their dedication and commitment.

tree_branches.name: Mr MATT CROSS

tree_branches.name: Community Bank Lindfield Grants
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Community Bank Lindfield Grants
tree_branches.text: Mr MATT CROSS ( Davidson ) —On Tuesday 11 November, Community Bank Lindfield hosted the Staff and Directors Grants Night. Every year, each member of the Community Bank Lindfield team is given $1000 to donate to a community group of their choice, a chance to personally give back and recognise the wonderful organisations that strengthen our community. This year's recipients included the NORTH Foundation, Community Flower Studio, SUNS Pickleball, Ku-ring-gai Neighbourhood Centre, EPIC, Hornsby Connect, the Cavalcade of History and Fashion, KYDS Youth Counselling, Ku-ring-gai Community Workshop, Ku-ring-gai Netball Association, San Foundation, North Shore Mums Smiles2U, the Hornsby Ku-ring-gai Women's Shelter, NextSense, The Dish of St John's, Computer Pals for Seniors Turramurra, and Friends of Ku-ring-gai Environment. This is a simple yet powerful way to give back and to recognise the local groups that contribute to our community. I thank Community Bank Lindfield and its staff for their generosity and for the positive impact they make across our local area.

tree_branches.name: Mr MATT CROSS

tree_branches.name: Model Global Parliament 2025
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Model Global Parliament 2025
tree_branches.text: Mr MATT CROSS ( Davidson ) —On Monday 10 November, I had the pleasure of addressing the 2025 Model Global Parliament at the Parliament of New South Wales. The Model Global Parliament, an initiative of the Institute for Global Peace and Sustainable Governance, gives students the opportunity to experience a simulated global parliament and debate real-world issues, developing their decision-making and leadership skills. I was deeply impressed by how thoughtfully the students engaged with complex global challenges and proposed constructive, compassionate solutions. It was wonderful to see them demonstrate such enthusiasm and insight. I recognise Dr Zeny Edwards OAM for all her work in bringing students together and helping them reach their full potential. The work you do is life changing.

tree_branches.name: Mr MATT CROSS
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Model Global Parliament 2025 > Mr MATT CROSS

tree_branches.name: St Paul's Students Kicking Goals Abroad
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > St Paul's Students Kicking Goals Abroad
tree_branches.text: Mr MICHAEL KEMP ( Oxley ) —Congratulations to St Paul's students, Dane F., Ethan F. and Wolfe H., who have achieved an incredible milestone in their selection to attend the West Ham United Development Tour in the United Kingdom. This is a rare opportunity, offered only to a handful of talented young players who have shown outstanding skill, determination, and sportsmanship. While in the UK, Dane, Ethan and Wolfe will take part in six elite coaching clinics with clubs in London, Manchester and Edinburgh, all with the English Premier League. They'll also experience the thrill of five live Premier League matches, learning from some of the world's best players and coaches. Their selection reflects not only their hard work on the field but also the unwavering support of their families, coaches and the St Paul's community who have helped them reach this moment. It's a chance to learn, grow, and represent their school and region with pride on the international stage. I wish Dane, Ethan and Wolfe every success on this exciting journey. Go out there, give it everything, and make the most of every moment!

tree_branches.name: Mr MICHAEL KEMP

tree_branches.name: Khloe Vale Receives Youth of the Year Award
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Khloe Vale Receives Youth of the Year Award
tree_branches.text: Mr MICHAEL KEMP ( Oxley ) —Congratulations to Kempsey High School's Year 9 student, Khloe Vale, recipient of the Youth of the Year Award at the NASCA 2025 Youth Awards night. This prestigious honour is awarded to young Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander students who demonstrate excellence not just in academics or sport, but through leadership, community engagement and a deep connection to culture. Khloe embodies these values, leading with integrity and representing her peers with pride. Khloe's recognition doesn't stop there. This year, she was also selected to represent Connected Communities on the Minister's Student Council, one of only 27 students from across NSW chosen to work directly with the Education Secretary and Minister for Education. This role ensures that student voices are heard in shaping the future of public education, and Khloe's inclusion speaks volumes about her leadership and commitment to positive change. I congratulate Khloe on these outstanding achievements and commend her for being an inspiring example of how connection to culture, identity and community can drive success. I look forward to seeing her continued contributions to Kempsey High and beyond.

tree_branches.name: Mr MICHAEL KEMP

tree_branches.name: Brydi's Brilliant Ride
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Brydi's Brilliant Ride
tree_branches.text: Mr MICHAEL KEMP ( Oxley ) —What an outstanding effort from Dorrigo High School's very own Brydi Fittock, who recently represented her school and community with pride at the Inter-Schools Horse Extravaganza (ISHE) in Tamworth. Brydi and her horse, Sarah Fene Raine, took to the arena in the dressage and senior 60cm show jumping events, competing against talented riders from schools right across the state. It's no small feat stepping into such a high-pressure competition, but Brydi showed incredible composure and determination, achieving an impressive third place after jumping a clear round in both Round 1 and the jump off! Representing Dorrigo High on a stage like ISHE is about more than just results. It's about courage, commitment, and the passion that drives young people like Brydi to give their best, even when the stakes are high and the nerves are real. Her success is a wonderful reflection of the strong community spirit that defines Dorrigo, where hard work, teamwork and a love for horses run deep. Congratulations, Brydi, on this fantastic achievement. You've made your school, your community, and everyone back home incredibly proud.

tree_branches.name: Mr MICHAEL KEMP

tree_branches.name: Arini Kazi
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Arini Kazi
tree_branches.text: Mr DUGALD SAUNDERS ( Dubbo ) —Speaker, I would like to recognise Dubbo South Public student, Arini Kazi, who has been named on the merit list of international writing competition Kids World Travel Guide Essay competition. The international essay writing competition had the theme "My World Our Future" and received 424 entries from young writers across 53 countries. Essays showcased a wide range of writing styles, from analytical and factual, to imaginative and emotional, reflecting the diverse voices of young thinkers around the world. Not only was Arini named on the merit list, but she was impressively the only Australian student to earn a place on it! This marks the first time Dubbo South Public School has participated in an international competition, making Arini's achievement even more remarkable. She has proudly represented Dubbo South Public School, Dubbo and Australia on the world stage. Her success is a celebration of her creativity and courage. As a Year Five student, and already demonstrating a strong ability to challenge herself, think globally and using her voice to share ideas, Arini has a bright future ahead. Congratulations Arini, keep up the great work!

tree_branches.name: Mr DUGALD SAUNDERS
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Arini Kazi > Mr DUGALD SAUNDERS

tree_branches.name: Gillian Ryan
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Gillian Ryan
tree_branches.text: Mr DUGALD SAUNDERS ( Dubbo ) —Speaker, I would like to recognise Gillian Ryan who was presented with Life Membership of the Wellington Race Club at their November 16 Race meeting. Gillian is a stalwart of the club, having volunteered for many decades. Not only has Gillian been a hard worker on race club committees, but she has also contributed tirelessly behind the scenes. In fact, she has witnessed enormous changes across the industry, as well as the way committees and clubs are run. When she first sought to join the Wellington committee, she was told they didn't allow women, today women are the backbone of many country race clubs, including Gillian! Being told no didn't deter her. With the support of other dedicated women, she helped raise vital funds for the club by selling raffle tickets for bull raffles, merino rams, and in later years, young horses. Once she secured a place on the committee, her commitment only grew. She was often found working in the canteen, and on one memorable race day she and another volunteer sold over one thousand hot dogs! Congratulations Gillian on this prestigious recognition of all your hard work and dedication to the Wellington Race Club.

tree_branches.name: Mr DUGALD SAUNDERS
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Gillian Ryan > Mr DUGALD SAUNDERS

tree_branches.name: Anne Elliott
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Anne Elliott
tree_branches.text: Mr DUGALD SAUNDERS ( Dubbo ) —Speaker, I would like to recognise Anne Elliott who has been awarded the 2025 JR Muller Award for Promotion and Marketing by Gliding Australia. Each year Gliding Australia take the opportunity to celebrate individuals who lift the sport higher though dedication, innovation and service. Those whose contributions ensure the community continues to thrive. Anne has earned a reputation for celebrating gliding with passion and consistency. She is an administrator of multiple gliding Facebook pages where shares daily stories, news and historical treasures with both Australian and international audiences. Her engaging posts help broaden the reach of Gliding Australia, sparking enthusiasm for the sport among pilots and non-pilots alike. This is not the first time Anne's outstanding work in promoting gliding has been recognised, she was also the winner of this award in 2009, further highlighting her enduring talent and passion for the sport. Locally, Anne is a dedicated and passionate member and Patron of the Narromine Aero Club. A true community gem, when she is not promoting and sharing her love of gliding, she lends her time and expertise to other local organisations such as Narromine Cottage Craft. Congratulations Anne on this well-deserved recognition!

tree_branches.name: Mr DUGALD SAUNDERS

tree_branches.name: Lismore High Campus A Premier's Award Finalist
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Lismore High Campus A Premier's Award Finalist
tree_branches.text: Ms JANELLE SAFFIN ( Lismore — Minister for Small Business, Minister for Recovery, and Minister for the North Coast ) —I WISH to congratulate The Rivers Secondary College – Lismore High Campus on being named a finalist in the Delivering world-class education and training category of the 2025 NSW Premier's Awards, recognising excellence in public service delivery. The school featured for its Tiny Homes @ Lismore High: Building Futures One Tiny Home at a Time project. This is an innovative, alternate learning program in which Stage 5 students (Years 9 and 10) at Lismore High Campus (LHC) design and construct a tiny home with the guidance of staff and local industry professionals. Developed in partnership with RIEP (Regional Industry Education Partnerships), who also provided the initial seed funding, the project delivers hands-on, trade-based education designed to build skills, confidence and community. In 2025, the project culminated in the successful sale of the completed 2024 Tiny Home for $65,000, allowing the initiative to become a self-sustaining, legacy project. The program directly contributes to improved student engagement, attendance, and post-school outcomes, all while fostering community partnerships and providing meaningful learning beyond the classroom. I again congratulate Lismore High Campus teachers, students and industry mentors on the outstanding success of a program which is providing affordable housing.

tree_branches.name: Ms JANELLE SAFFIN
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Lismore High Campus A Premier's Award Finalist > Ms JANELLE SAFFIN

tree_branches.name: Northern NSW Lhd A Premier's Award Finalist
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Northern NSW Lhd A Premier's Award Finalist
tree_branches.text: Ms JANELLE SAFFIN ( Lismore — Minister for Small Business, Minister for Recovery, and Minister for the North Coast ) —I WISH to congratulate the Northern NSW Local Health District on being named a finalist in the Delivering world-class education and training category of the 2025 NSW Premier's Awards, recognising excellence in public service delivery. The NNSWLHD faced the urgent challenge of addressing regional health inequities and an ageing population while building a future-ready, skilled workforce. In response, Southern Cross University, TAFE NSW, Bond University and Griffith University came together to form the Northern NSW Academic Health Alliance (NAHA), partnering with NNSWLHD to co-design a transformative, sustainable model of health education, research, and workforce development. This first-of-its-kind partnership created a NAHA-funded, dedicated floor in the state-of-the-art Learning, Development and Research Building at Tweed Valley Hospital, where students train in real clinical settings and staff advance research and teaching. The model preserves each partner's autonomy while driving shared outcomes to build a skilled workforce tailored to regional needs. Focused on long-term sustainability through a 15-year agreement, the Alliance aligns closely with the NSW Higher Education Strategy 2025–2029, proactively anticipating and shaping the healthcare workforce of tomorrow. The category was won by TAFE NSW partnering with Woolworths to provide pathways for students with disability.

tree_branches.name: Ms JANELLE SAFFIN
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Northern NSW Lhd A Premier's Award Finalist > Ms JANELLE SAFFIN

tree_branches.name: Richmond Riverkeeper Honoured at NSW Coastal Conference
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Richmond Riverkeeper Honoured at NSW Coastal Conference
tree_branches.text: Ms JANELLE SAFFIN ( Lismore — Minister for Small Business, Minister for Recovery, and Minister for the North Coast ) —I WISH to congratulate Richmond Riverkeeper Kristin den Exter who was named winner of the Local Hero category at the 2025 NSW Coastal Conference Awards in Ballina recently. Kristin was recognised for her outstanding contribution to river health, community consultation, and coastal care. The award acknowledges Kristin's leadership through Richmond Riverkeeper and the Richmond RiverFest, a month-long celebration of culture, community and Country that connects people from the sea to the source. I have followed the work of the Richmond Riverkeepers closely and receive regular updates from them. Associate Professor in History at Southern Cross University and fellow Richmond Riverkeeper Adele Wessell told The Lismore App: "Kristen has been listening to what the river is telling us her whole life, listing to the knowledge of Custodians and First Peoples and committing herself to a lifetime of working with the river with integrity and love in a way that inspires everyone around her," Associate Professor Wessell said. For her part, Kristen spoke of collective effort: "From Elders and artists to scientists and volunteers, we're all working together so that the rivers of the Richmond catchment can one day be drinkable, swimmable and fishable again."

tree_branches.name: Ms JANELLE SAFFIN

tree_branches.name: Liam Rees is A Rising Star
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Liam Rees is A Rising Star
tree_branches.text: Ms STEPH C OOKE ( Cootamundra ) —I would like to extend my heartfelt congratulations to Liam Rees, a first-year electrotechnology apprentice, on recently being named the 2025 Audi Foundation–Country Education Foundation Rising Star Award recipient. This prestigious honour recognises young people who demonstrate exceptional commitment, perseverance, and community spirit. Liam's dedication to his Certificate III in Electrotechnology at TAFE Wagga Wagga, along with his ability to balance work, study, sport, and family life, is truly inspiring. His positive attitude, strong work ethic, and determination to succeed have not only impressed his peers but also made him a role model for others in our community. Through the support of the Country Education Foundation of Cootamundra, Liam has been able to ease the financial pressures of his apprenticeship by purchasing the essential tools needed for his trade. His gratitude and ongoing connection to regional Australia highlight his commitment to giving back and supporting others who follow in his footsteps. Liam's achievement is a testament to his hard work, character, and bright future in the electrical industry. We are incredibly proud of his success and look forward to seeing all he accomplishes in the years ahead.

tree_branches.name: Murrumburrah Public School Agriculture Department and Students
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Murrumburrah Public School Agriculture Department and Students
tree_branches.text: Ms STEPH COOKE ( Cootamundra ) —I would like to recognise the Murrumburrah High School Agriculture Department and their students for their continued success and commitment in striving for excellence in agriculture. From participating in wool, to fruit and veg, grain, beef and meat sheep competitions across the region, there are no limits to what these students have been able to achieve. This doesn't come without huge efforts from people like Head of Agriculture and Science Department and Deputy Principal, Jan Young who has been passionately championing this program for many years and continues its development to meet the ever-changing needs of the future. The current teaching staff Kirsten Pack, Grace Armour and Zoe McCarthy and of course, the expertise and support of community members such as Harvey Jones, Marg and Graham Taylor, Steve Phillips and Sam Hunter, ensure this valuable education meets the current and future needs of students interested in Agriculture. On a recent visit to the school, I experienced their efforts in tackling the global challenge of food insecurity, thanks to an innovative partnership with Food Ladder. I commend all past and present teaching staff and students on their commitment and achievements.

tree_branches.name: Ms STEPH COOKE

tree_branches.name: Cowra Jersey Day Golf Event
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Cowra Jersey Day Golf Event
tree_branches.text: Ms STEPH COOKE ( Cootamundra ) —Congratulations to the Cowra Golf Club and Julie and Mark Tucker for hosting another hugely successful Jersey Golf Day event to raise awareness for organ and tissue donation. Participants were encouraged to wear their favourite sports jersey as part of the National Jersey Day Organ Donation Awareness initiative, combining community spirit, sport, and an important message about the gift of life. Julie and Mark Tucker have shown remarkable strength and compassion following the unimaginable loss of their beloved son, Brady, in 2021. Through their grief and inspired by Brady's love of golf and his selfless act of organ donation, they have dedicated themselves to increasing awareness about the importance and life-changing impact of organ donation. This annual event continues to grow each year, showcasing the Cowra and golfing communities' generosity, unity, and commitment to supporting meaningful causes. I extend my congratulations to all who helped organise the day and to everyone who participated. This event not only raises vital awareness for organ and tissue donation but also honours Brady's memory and the enduring impact of his life on family, friends, and those who received his precious gift of life.

tree_branches.name: Ms STEPH COOKE

tree_branches.name: Sisterly Bites
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Sisterly Bites
tree_branches.text: Mrs TINA AYYAD ( Holsworthy ) —I'd like to acknowledge Sisterly Bites, a local business founded by sisters Rose and Nancy Daoud, whose generosity and community spirit extend far beyond their kitchen. What began as a small home project has grown into one of Sydney's most loved healthy snack brands, but what truly sets them apart is their commitment to giving back. Through their charity work, Sisterly Bites has supported vital causes such as the Breast Cancer Foundation, the Melanoma Institute of Australia, and local families at the Randwick Family Centre, donating treats to Defence Force mums and families. They've also partnered with St Merkorious Charity to help feed those doing it tough, showing their deep compassion for others. As a proudly female-founded business, Rose and Nancy empower women through collaboration and community workshops, inspiring health, creativity, and connection. Beyond their business, they personally dedicate time and resources to helping the homeless, support church initiatives, and raise awareness for the Leukaemia Foundation's Light the Night Walk. Their efforts have not gone unnoticed, Sisterly Bites received the Canterbury-Bankstown Chamber of Commerce Small Business Month Award 2025 and were named Finalists in the Australian Women's Small Business Champion Awards 2025.

tree_branches.name: Mrs TINA AYYAD

tree_branches.name: Deborah Engeler
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Deborah Engeler
tree_branches.text: Mrs TINA AYYAD ( Holsworthy ) —I would like to acknowledge Ms Deborah Engeler for her outstanding and long-term contribution to the Illawong Athletics community. Deborah first became involved with Illawong Athletics in 1996 and from those early days as a parent helper, she quickly became an active member of the committee, taking on numerous roles including Vice President for three years and President for seven years. In 2008, while still serving on the Little Athletics committee, Deborah was invited to join the Illawong Athletics Inc. Board, where she has now served for many years, including the last eight years as Chair. Deborah's commitment to the sport extends well beyond administration. She joined the Illawong Revesby Workers Athletics Club as an athlete in 2002 and continues to compete today. She has also served on the senior club committee, ensuring the ongoing success and growth of athletics in the local community. In addition to her club roles, Deborah is an Athletics NSW official, regularly officiating at meets between her own events, and a proud member of NSW Masters Athletics. I thank and congratulate her for her remarkable service and dedication.

tree_branches.name: Mrs TINA AYYAD

tree_branches.name: Pak-Aus Engineers Association
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Pak-Aus Engineers Association
tree_branches.text: Mrs TINA AYYAD ( Holsworthy ) —I would like to acknowledge the Pak-Aus Engineers Association for their remarkable contribution to Australia's engineering community and for their ongoing commitment to excellence, mentorship, and multicultural collaboration. The Association continues to build strong professional and cultural bridges between Pakistani and Australian engineers, fostering innovation, opportunity, and shared growth. This year's annual function was a celebration of dedication and achievement, honouring those who have made outstanding contributions across their fields. Azhar Nasir, Behram Pestonji, Hamid Khan, Nabeel Khan, Shahid Javed, and Shakeel Ahmed were recognised for over 25 years of distinguished engineering service. Mr. Tariq Mahmood Mirza received the Lifetime Achievement Award for his contribution to Urdu literature, Dr. Ishrat Ali for community service, and Mr. Abdul Razzak Lakhani for engineering excellence. Distinguished Professor Dr. Rahat Munir, Consul General Mr. Qamar Zaman, and High Commissioner Mr. Irfan Shaukat were also honoured with Special Recognition Awards for their exceptional leadership and support. Led by President Insaf Khan and the executive committee, the Association exemplifies how professional expertise, cultural pride, and community service can come together to build a stronger, more connected Australia.

tree_branches.name: Mrs TINA AYYAD

tree_branches.name: Regentville Rural Fire Brigade
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Regentville Rural Fire Brigade
tree_branches.text: Mrs TANYA DAVIES ( Badgerys Creek ) —I express my sincere thanks to Regentville Rural Fire Brigade for providing the community with information to help protect their family and property this upcoming bush fire season, at its recent, annual open day, the Get Ready Weekend. There was a great turnout from the community, who got to learn more about what the RFS does, see RFS trucks on display, join in activities for kids and join in an enticing BBQ. The newly formed and Sydney-based Volunteer Rescue Association (VRA) Squad demonstrated some of their rescue skills to the attendees. I encourage everyone in the community to prepare a bushfire survival plan. I recognise the important efforts of the RFS, for their ongoing education of the community in fire safety, and for putting their own safety on the line to fight fires.

tree_branches.name: Xavier Curmi
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Xavier Curmi
tree_branches.text: Mrs TANYA DAVIES ( Badgerys Creek ) —Congratulations to Glenmore Park High School student, Xavier Curmi, a Motorcycle racer from Wallacia, who has had an amazing season in his debut year at the Junior Cup. Whilst a bLU cRU Oceania Cup rookie, Xavier fought hard to achieve 2nd place for the final Oceania Junior Cup round of 2025. Not only did Xavier finish 2nd for the round that included another race win, he also finished 4th for the year in the final championship. I look forward to following Xavier's progress and achievements as he moves up to a higher category of racing in 2026. I commend and congratulate all the team at Xavier Curmi AX Racing.

tree_branches.name: Oran Park Hockey Club
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Oran Park Hockey Club
tree_branches.text: Mrs TANYA DAVIES ( Badgerys Creek ) —On behalf of my electorate of Badgerys Creek, I congratulate Oran Park Hockey Club for a very successful 2025 season, the most successful in its history. The club fielded 166 players across 15 teams, within various age groups, in the Metropolitan South West Association (MSWA) competition. Four of the club's teams qualified for the finals; the 3rd Grade Men, Under 12's Juniors, Under 10's Lightnings, and B Grade Ladies. Out of the four finalists, the Under 10's Lightnings and B Grade Ladies qualified for the Grand Finals, which were held on 26 September 2025. The club is to also be commended for its junior development, with 21 players participating in the MSWA Development carnivals and 11 players competing in the State Championships. I wish the club continued success as they look ahead to season 2026.

tree_branches.name: Mrs TANYA DAVIES

tree_branches.name: Wyanga Aboriginal Aged Care
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Wyanga Aboriginal Aged Care
tree_branches.text: Ms JENNY LEONG ( New town ) —On behalf of the Newtown electorate, I would like to congratulate Wyanga Aboriginal Aged Care on their successful Community Building Partnership grant application and acknowledge their important work supporting local Aboriginal Elders to live independently and stay connected to their community. Wyanga are a not-for-profit Aboriginal-led aged care provider supporting Elders across inner-Sydney. Through their work they ensure that Elders in our community can access culturally safe care and support. Wyanga will use the funds to modify their existing vehicle to ensure that it is safe for wheelchair users to access. This will provide safe, inclusive transport for Elders, significantly enhancing participation in community activities, attending medical appointments, community programs, and essential services, improving mobility, independence, and wellbeing. It is so important that all members of our community at every age can access the care they need and are supported to be connected to their friends, family and community – and this grant will do just that. I thank Wyanga for their important work providing care, support and community connection for Elders in our community.

tree_branches.name: Ms JENNY LEONG
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Wyanga Aboriginal Aged Care > Ms JENNY LEONG

tree_branches.name: Australian Railway Historical Society
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Australian Railway Historical Society
tree_branches.text: Ms JENNY LEONG ( Newtown ) —On behalf of the Newtown electorate, I would like to congratulate the Australian Railway Historical Society for their successful 2025 Community Building Partnership grant. For almost a century, the dedicated team at the Australian Railway Historical Society in Alexandria has shared the wonderful and exciting history of railways with our community. They are caretakers of a large collection of historically significant archival material that holds the history of Australia's railways and chronicles the importance of railways to communities across this continent. The dedicated people involved in the Australian Railway Historical Society will use the funding to replace ageing scanners and computer equipment. This will support the Society to continue their work digitising archival material so that it can be shared with the community now and for generations to come. I thank the Australian Railway Historical Society for their enthusiasm and their commitment to sharing the joy of railways with the Newtown community.

tree_branches.name: Ms JENNY LEONG
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Australian Railway Historical Society > Ms JENNY LEONG

tree_branches.name: Camdenville Public School P&C Association
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Camdenville Public School P&C Association
tree_branches.text: Ms JENNY LEONG ( Newtown ) —On behalf of the Newtown electorate, I would like to congratulate the Camdenville P&C Association for their successful 2025 Community Building Partnership grant and thank them for their work supporting the Camdenville Public School learning community. The P&C will use this grant to complete improvements to the school's outdoor learning space by installing platforms, a wobble bridge, and a log ladder. These improvements will ensure all students have access to an inclusive and fun playground area. Outdoor learning areas are crucial in ensuring that young people have access to a healthy and well-rounded education, supporting them to be active as young people and throughout their lives. I thank the Camdenville P&C Association for them commitment to ensuring that young people in our community have access to fun and inclusive outdoor areas for learning and play and acknowledge their tireless efforts supporting teachers and young learners in our community.

tree_branches.name: Ms JENNY LEONG
