tree_branches.name: Elizabeth Guthrie
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Elizabeth Guthrie
tree_branches.text: Ms JACQUI SCRUBY ( Pittwater ) —Elizabeth Guthrie is a talented local writer whose short story was recently selected for publication in the 2024 Seniors Stories Anthology, an annual collection distributed to libraries across New South Wales that celebrates the creativity of older writers. Elizabeth's story, written for the competition theme "Then and Now", was chosen among the top 100 entries. This is a great achievement that reflects her growing skill and passion for storytelling. Since retiring, Elizabeth has embraced her love of writing, joining the Northern Beaches Writers Group where she continues to hone her craft and share stories that capture imagination and emotion. Beyond her writing, Elizabeth is also a dedicated volunteer at the Northern Beaches Women's Shelter, where she contributes to an organisation that provides vital support to women in need. Elizabeth's creativity, compassion and community spirit exemplify the very best of Pittwater. I congratulate her on this wonderful recognition and thank her for her contribution to our local community.

tree_branches.name: Ms JACQUI SCRUBY
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Elizabeth Guthrie > Ms JACQUI SCRUBY

tree_branches.name: Associate Professor Richard West
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Associate Professor Richard West
tree_branches.text: Ms JACQUI SCRUBY ( Pittwater ) —Today I recognise Associate Professor Richard West, who is retiring after more than a decade as President of the Palm Beach Whale Beach Association. During this time, he has remained committed to preserving the natural beauty and residential amenity of our area. A/Prof West has been a highly effective advocate across all levels of government. Under his leadership he has protected many conservation zonings in the local area, and he led the successful campaign against commercial development on culturally significant Barrenjoey Headland. He has championed long-overdue improvements to Governor Phillip Park, supported multiple submissions against inappropriate development, and advocated for repairs to local rock pools. He has also been a strong voice for completing the Manly to Palm Beach Coastal Walkway, improving road and pedestrian safety, keeping Avalon and Newport out of the Transport Oriented Development plan, and ending the Public Private Partnership model for Northern Beaches Hospital. A/Prof West's broader life has also been one of leadership - as a general and trauma surgeon, a founder of the Sydney Breast Cancer Foundation and a key figure behind Australia's national breast-screening program. I thank him for his exceptional dedication to our community.

tree_branches.name: Ms JACQUI SCRUBY
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Associate Professor Richard West > Ms JACQUI SCRUBY

tree_branches.name: Patricia Fry
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Patricia Fry
tree_branches.text: Ms JACQUI SCRUBY ( Pittwater ) —Today I recognise Patsy Fry of Newport, whose creativity and persistence have brought colour and character to our Newport village. Patsy has lived in Newport for 30 years and has spent much of that time finding practical, community-minded ways to improve the place she loves. When she saw Newport needed more vibrancy, she took action, working with Northern Beaches Council to deliver the fairy lights that now brighten Robertson Road. More recently, Patsy has been the driving force behind Newport's unique stump planters. After seeing a tree removed on Queens Parade, she salvaged the stump, carved it by hand over 16 weeks and transformed it into a natural planter filled with geraniums. With support from generous locals, she has installed several more and is already working on the next set, hoping this becomes a defining feature for the village. Patsy also co-founded the Newport Sculpture Trail, engaging 35 local shops and bringing art, music and performance to the community. Patsy's passion, patience and commitment have left a lasting mark on Newport. I thank Patsy for her imagination, hard work and love for our community.

tree_branches.name: Ms JACQUI SCRUBY
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Patricia Fry > Ms JACQUI SCRUBY

tree_branches.name: May Gibbs - Gumnut Fair 2025
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > May Gibbs - Gumnut Fair 2025
tree_branches.text: Ms FELICITY WILSON ( North Shore ) —Congratulations to May Gibbs' Nutcote on celebrating their 100 years by bringing our community together at their annual Gumnut Fair. This year was especially significant as it marked a century of storytelling, creativity and community spirit. Each year, our community steps into the enchanting world of May Gibbs and celebrates her extraordinary legacy through a day of family-friendly fun. This year's Gumnut Fair created a joyful atmosphere for all ages, with families - including mine - enjoying the May Gibbs raffle and prize wheel, roving Gumnut characters, creative children's activities, and treats including a bake sale, sausage sizzle, and the famous scones with jam and cream. You could begin Christmas shopping with a beautiful selection of May Gibbs and Australian-themed gifts or join a guided tour of the historic house. I extend my sincere thanks to the Nutcote Board, led by Chair Sonia Beth Berry, Nutcote Manager Megan Sadler and all volunteers for their dedication to this cherished monument. The Gumnut Fair is Nutcote's largest annual fundraiser, and their combined efforts ensure this community treasure continues to thrive for generations to come.

tree_branches.name: Ms FELICITY WILSON
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > May Gibbs - Gumnut Fair 2025 > Ms FELICITY WILSON

tree_branches.name: Kirribilli Street Festival
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Kirribilli Street Festival
tree_branches.text: Ms FELICITY WILSON ( North Shore ) —I recognise the community of Kirribilli for bringing Broughton Street alive with the sound of live music and families enjoying an all-day free event of food, music and culture at the inaugural Kirribilli Street Festival. On Saturday, 16 November, the streets of Kirribilli swapped cars for people with the major attraction of the pop-up roller rink in the Burton Street Tunnel. The disco-themed roller rink was a unique opportunity to skate under the Sydney Harbour Bridge – which my kids and I joined in (with just a few bruises to show for it!) I recognise the Sydney Street Choir, Loud and Proud Choir and Neutral Bay's Hummingbird Adult Pop Choir and the Ensemble Theatre who performed, and all the circus, street theatre and live performances. I also acknowledge the stall holders, and Kirribilli's cafes, restaurants and businesses such as Grace of India and Bloomingales who opened their doors and took to the streets with alfresco dining and workshops, truly making Broughton Street alive and welcoming. We loved joining in the festivities as everyone came together to celebrate everything that makes Kirribilli such a vibrant and connected community.

tree_branches.name: Ms FELICITY WILSON
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Kirribilli Street Festival > Ms FELICITY WILSON

tree_branches.name: Middle Harbour Public School Carnival Returns
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Middle Harbour Public School Carnival Returns
tree_branches.text: Ms FELICITY WILSON ( North Shore ) —I congratulate Middle Harbour Public School's Carnival for holding their Middle Harbour Public School Carnival. After a six-year hiatus, Middle Harbour Public School's P&C brought back the carnival, which is both a fundraiser and community event, and a must-attend event for all families and residents. Over 3,000 guests registered to attend, and the Carnival had a petting zoo, a giant slide, spinning tea cups, ponies and plenty of games for kids and adults to enjoy. There was great food on offer, including sausage sizzles and chips on a stick. There was also an assortment of craft goods and second-hand treasures to purchase. I acknowledge P&C President Dana Lightbody, Treasurer Andrea Voight, Secretary Carl Bunn and Committee Members Sarah Jarrett, Joanne De La Mar, and Carlotta Annan for their commitment and dedication, and for bringing back this iconic and well-loved event. I recognise Middle Harbour Public School Principal Laura Barry for her ongoing leadership and congratulate Middle Harbour Public School on their carnival.

tree_branches.name: 80th Anniversary of Peats Ferry Bridge
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > 80th Anniversary of Peats Ferry Bridge
tree_branches.text: Mr JAMES WALLACE ( Hornsby ) —Last Saturday, the 15th of November, our community came together to celebrate the 80th anniversary of one of our region's most significant pieces of infrastructure, the Peats Ferry Bridge. It was wonderful to see residents marking this milestone and reflecting on the role the bridge has played in shaping life across our area. Opened in 1945, the bridge transformed daily life for communities along the Hawkesbury River. By replacing the long-running ferry service, it created a permanent and reliable link between the Central Coast and the Hornsby district, supporting families, workers, emergency services and local businesses for generations. This anniversary is an important opportunity to acknowledge the planners, designers and workers who built the Peats Ferry Bridge during a period marked by hardship, rationing and the final years of the Second World War. Their work delivered a structure that has stood strong for eighty years and continues to play a vital role in our region today. The Peats Ferry Bridge remains a symbol of connection and resilience, and we extend our thanks to all who have maintained and preserved this essential link across the Hawkesbury.

tree_branches.name: 24-Hour Aed for Berowra
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > 24-Hour Aed for Berowra
tree_branches.text: Mr JAMES WALLACE ( Hornsby ) —I recognise the generous donation of a new 24-hour accessible Automated External Defibrillator, or AED, for the Berowra community. This lifesaving device has been gifted by Shelby Formosa and her family. Shelby is a paramedic whose commitment to strengthening community safety is truly commendable. Their generosity reflects the best of our local spirit and a genuine desire to protect others in moments of need. The AED has also been registered with the GoodSAM app, which allows Triple Zero operators to guide callers to the nearest available defibrillator during a cardiac emergency. This simple but powerful tool ensures that lifesaving equipment can be found quickly, helping community members act with confidence when every second matters. Modern AEDs provide clear voice instructions and are designed so that anyone, regardless of medical training, can use them safely and effectively. Having a device available around the clock significantly increases the chances of survival in the event of sudden cardiac arrest and gives our community an important additional layer of protection.

tree_branches.name: Mr JAMES WALLACE

tree_branches.name: Studio Artes Christmas Cards
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Studio Artes Christmas Cards
tree_branches.text: Mr JAMES WALLACE ( Hornsby ) —I acknowledge and thank Studio ARTES for generously supplying this year's Christmas cards for our community. Studio ARTES has long been recognised for its outstanding work in providing creative programs, social connection and opportunities for people with disability. Their contribution of beautifully designed Christmas cards continues this tradition of creativity and community spirit. Each card features original artwork created by Studio ARTES artists Matthew Ye and Kate Beckerleg, whose talent and imagination shine through. Their vibrant underwater designs are filled with colourful fish, playful sea creatures and bold ocean scenes, bringing a sense of fun and creativity to the festive season. It is wonderful to see local artists sharing such joyful work with the community. Studio ARTES plays an important role in supporting individuals to express themselves, develop new skills and build confidence through the arts. I thank Studio ARTES, their dedicated staff and their talented artists for this thoughtful contribution. Their creativity brings our community together and adds a unique, uplifting touch to our celebrations during this festive season.

Moses competed in the NSW CHS State Athletics Championships this year, winning 3 medals: 2nd in 3000m, 2nd in 1500m and first in 800m. On behalf of the Shellharbour electorate, I congratulate Moses for this fantastic achievement and wish him the very best in his athletics career.

tree_branches.name: Police Dog, Yoyo
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Police Dog, Yoyo
tree_branches.text: Ms ANNA WATSON ( Shellharbour ) —I would like to acknowledge the service of Police Dog Yoyo, having served for 6 years and now retiring. Yoyo was born in 2018 as part of the Police Dog Unit. Yoyo has been an integral member of the team. Alongside his handler, Senior Constable Ward, he has patrolled across Lake Illawarra, Wollongong and the far south coast with unwavering dedication. On behalf of the Shellharbour electorate, I congratulate Yoyo on his service career. He can now hang up his harness for a well deserved retirement.

tree_branches.text: Ms ANNA WATSON ( Shellharbour ) —Congratulations to Rainer Schilder from Dapto High School on being crowned the Under-17 Australian Middleweight Champion. At just 15 years of age, Rainer Schilder's achievement in winning the Under-17 Australian Middleweight Championship is truly outstanding. His determination, discipline, and self-belief have set an inspiring example for young athletes across our community. On behalf of the Shellharbour electorate, please know the community is incredibly proud of your remarkable achievement and the bright future ahead of you.

tree_branches.name: Janette Hyde, OAM
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Janette Hyde, OAM
tree_branches.text: Mr ROBERT DWYER ( Port Macquarie ) —It gives me great pleasure to acknowledge Janette Hyde OAM, from Greater Port Macquarie Tourism Association, for her outstanding contribution over the past 15 years. Janette has been an integral part of the Association, dedicating her time, expertise, and passion to promoting our region as a premier tourism destination. In 2019, she was awarded the 'Dean Gorddard Award for Outstanding Contribution by an Individual to NSW' at the 2019 NSW State Tourism Awards. Her commitment has helped strengthen local tourism, foster community connections, and support countless initiatives that have showcased the beauty and vibrancy of Greater Port Macquarie. Beyond her professional achievements, Janette is known for her warmth, generosity, and unwavering support for colleagues and local businesses. Her ability to bring people together and her enthusiasm for every project have made her a beloved figure in our community. As Janette retires from her role, I extend my heartfelt gratitude for her years of service and dedication. Her legacy will continue to inspire future initiatives, reminding us of the power of community-driven tourism. I wish Janette all the best in her next chapter and thank her for everything she has done for the Port Macquarie region.

tree_branches.name: Mr ROBERT DWYER

tree_branches.name: Johns River Rural Fire Brigade
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-11-20) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Johns River Rural Fire Brigade
tree_branches.text: Mr ROBERT DWYER ( Port Macquarie ) —I wish to acknowledge and pay tribute to Johns River Rural Fire Brigade and its volunteers, whose dedication to protecting our community stands as a powerful example of selflessness and resilience. These men and women respond to bushfires, motor vehicle accidents, and severe weather events, often working in dangerous conditions to safeguard lives and property throughout the Port Macquarie-Hastings and Mid Coast areas. Their role is not only courageous, but also indispensable. The brigade provides a critical line of defence during bushfire season and beyond. In addition to emergency operations, they invest time in community engagement, training, and fire safety education, ensuring residents are informed and prepared. The benefits of their work extend far beyond immediate safety. By reducing the impact of disasters and aiding recovery, they help protect local businesses, tourism, and infrastructure. Their efforts also strengthen community spirit and resilience. I extend my sincere thanks to Captain Chris Bawn, Senior Deputy Captain Tim Gordon, Deputy Captain Simon Doyle, and every member of the Johns River Rural Fire Brigade for their commitment, bravery, and service. Their contribution makes our region safer, stronger, and better equipped to face future challenges.
